decisionNodes.stem: Which endovascular repair should have addressed {patientName}'s demonstrated leak?

answerChoices.label: Covered stent-graft bridging at the modular junction
answerChoices.rationale: A fabric gap provides a direct route into the sac. A covered bridge restores the missing barrier between the aligned components.

answerChoices.rationale: Expansion can improve apposition where fabric overlaps, but cannot supply the absent covering between separated ends.

answerChoices.rationale: Radial scaffolding does not add a covering across the demonstrated open channel to the sac.

answerChoices.rationale: The apparent increase uses different planes. Adequate source volumes permit a valid comparison before using enlargement to determine repair assessment.

decisionNodes.explanation: The reported 0.7-cm difference spans different measurement planes. Use the adequate acquired volumes to establish a matched comparison before interpreting growth. decisionNodes.stem: Which study should have completed {patientName}'s current aortic surveillance assessment?

answerChoices.label: MRI of the abdominal aorta
answerChoices.rationale: The current ultrasound does not define full sac size; MRI provides cross-sectional assessment without requiring the iodinated-contrast exposure implicated in his prior reaction.

answerChoices.rationale: Cross-sectional imaging addresses the inadequate ultrasound, but this proposed contrast examination disregards the serious prior immediate reaction when MRI is a supported alternative.

answerChoices.rationale: The prior success of ultrasound does not establish a usable current outer-wall measurement through the documented acoustic limitation.

decisionNodes.explanation: Current ultrasound adequacy matters more than the fact that ultrasound was useful previously. cases.learningSummary: Delayed branch-associated flow with an unchanged sac supports continued surveillance. A visible leak is not enough to choose its treatment; source and sac behavior matter. Do not carry forward a branch-leak label when a growing sac has an uncertain current inflow source. Problem-solving aortography can assess the attachments and modular junctions before choosing a branch-directed treatment. The problem is loss of covered continuity, not simply insufficient expansion. A covered bridge can close a separated modular junction. Balloon remodelling or bare-metal reinforcement addresses other apposition/support problems but does not itself cover a fabric gap.

decisionNodes.stem: Which left-subclavian strategy should have accompanied {patientName}'s elective TEVAR plan?

answerChoices.label: Carotid-subclavian bypass before aortic coverage
answerChoices.rationale: LSA interruption threatens inflow to the patent LIMA graft supplying an occluded native LAD territory.

answerChoices.label: Aortic coverage, then bypass if arm ischemia develops
answerChoices.rationale: An arm-symptom trigger does not protect the LIMA-dependent coronary circulation during elective coverage.

answerChoices.label: Carotid-subclavian transposition before aortic coverage
answerChoices.rationale: Transposition requires proximal subclavian clamping, which can interrupt the patent pedicled LIMA coronary inflow; bypass avoids that required interruption.

decisionNodes.explanation: Protect the pedicled LIMA coronary inflow before elective LSA coverage. Bypass avoids the proximal subclavian clamp required for transposition; waiting for arm ischemia also fails to protect this coronary-dependent territory.

answerChoices.rationale: The pattern points to spinal-cord perfusion injury; pressure support and reduction of intrathecal pressure address that mechanism.

answerChoices.distractorRationale: Cross-sectional imaging addresses the inadequate ultrasound, but this proposed contrast examination disregards the serious prior immediate reaction when MRI is a supported alternative.

answerChoices.label: Duplex ultrasound of the abdominal aorta
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The prior success of ultrasound does not establish a usable current outer-wall measurement through the documented acoustic limitation.

questions.explanation: Current ultrasound adequacy matters more than the fact that ultrasound was useful previously. Cross-sectional assessment is needed when the sac is not defined, and MRI is reasonable when CT is contraindicated. The earlier matched measurements do not establish the current sac size after an inadequate examination.

questions.stem: Which plan should have been selected for {patientName} during that admission?

answerChoices.label: Inpatient vascular assessment for aneurysm repair
Inpatient lumbar MRI before vascular assessment
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The unchanged structural spine finding does not establish that it explains the new rest pain and focal pain reproduced over the aorta.

answerChoices.label: Clinical observation with scheduled aortic ultrasound follow-up
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Routine observation and surveillance do not address the new aneurysm-localized symptoms simply because the scan shows no leak.

questions.explanation: The pain pattern and focal tenderness make the aneurysm clinically concerning even though MR imaging shows no extravasation. The unchanged lumbar finding does not by itself explain this new syndrome. Inpatient vascular repair assessment is appropriate; a size-based asymptomatic surveillance rule does not settle this admission.

questions.stem: Which aortic plan should have followed {patientName}'s measured result?

exhibit.caption: Constructed outside aortic ultrasound measurements

answerChoices.label: Arrange elective vascular repair assessment
Arrange aortic ultrasound in six months
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This can follow a male threshold applied to the full sac or a surveillance-only policy, but it postpones the supported female repair assessment here.

answerChoices.label: Arrange aortic ultrasound in twelve months
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The 4.2-cm flowing channel is not the aneurysm's full dimension used for the female surveillance band.

questions.explanation: Use the maximum outer-wall sac dimension. ACC/AHA recommends repair at the female size boundary, while SVS frames repair in the 5.0-5.4-cm range as a suggestion; both support specialist repair assessment in this supplied context. Neither diameter nor sex selects a procedure or removes the need to consider operative risk and patient goals.

questions.stem: Which pelvic-inflow strategy should have accompanied {patientName}'s planned distal seals?

answerChoices.label: Preserve right internal-iliac inflow during bilateral external-iliac extension
Preserve left internal-iliac inflow during bilateral external-iliac extension
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The left channel is already occluded; assigning preservation to that side does not protect the patent right pelvic supply from the planned coverage.

answerChoices.label: Exclude both internal-iliac origins during bilateral external-iliac extension
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This would intentionally interrupt the remaining right-sided route instead of preserving at least one direct hypogastric inflow when feasible.

questions.explanation: The current imaging leaves the right internal iliac as the remaining direct pelvic inflow. Preserve that route as part of exclusion planning when feasible. This is a strategy decision: the scan does not by itself establish eligibility for a particular iliac branch device, and the final preserving reconstruction requires separate anatomic planning.

questions.stem: Which plan should have followed {patientName}'s later surveillance study?

exhibit.caption: Constructed outside-record measurements; not a reproduced clinical image

answerChoices.label: Continue aortic duplex imaging surveillance
Embolize the lumbar inflow and sac cavity
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A visible branch leak does not by itself establish a treatment benefit when the sac is stable.

answerChoices.label: Extend the proximal seal with an aortic cuff
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The observed inflow is from lumbar branches, not the proximal attachment.

questions.explanation: Delayed branch-associated flow with an unchanged sac supports continued surveillance. A visible leak is not enough to choose its treatment; source and sac behavior matter.

questions.stem: Which angiographic assessment should precede targeted leak treatment for {patientName} now?

answerChoices.label: Aortography across the seal zones and graft junctions
Selective mesenteric-to-inferior-mesenteric collateral angiography
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This maps a branch route but does not resolve the possible attachment or component defect producing the current sac growth.

answerChoices.label: Selective iliolumbar-to-lumbar collateral angiography
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The lumbar branch near the contrast focus does not establish that it is the only source.

questions.explanation: Do not carry forward a branch-leak label when a growing sac has an uncertain current inflow source. Problem-solving aortography can assess the attachments and modular junctions before choosing a branch-directed treatment.

questions.stem: Which endovascular repair should have addressed {patientName}'s demonstrated leak?

answerChoices.label: Covered stent-graft bridging at the modular junction
Balloon remodelling at the modular junction
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Expansion can improve apposition where fabric overlaps, but cannot supply the absent covering between separated ends.

answerChoices.label: Bare-metal stent reinforcement at the leaking segment
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Radial scaffolding does not add a covering across the demonstrated open channel to the sac.

questions.explanation: The problem is loss of covered continuity, not simply insufficient expansion. A covered bridge can close a separated modular junction. Balloon remodelling or bare-metal reinforcement addresses other apposition/support problems but does not itself cover a fabric gap.

questions.stem: Which plan should have followed {patientName}'s proximal attachment finding?

answerChoices.label: Extend the proximal seal with an aortic cuff
Continue aortic duplex imaging surveillance
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Stable sac size does not justify observation of an established late direct attachment leak.

answerChoices.label: Embolize the lumbar inflow and sac cavity
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The demonstrated source is the proximal attachment, not a side branch.

questions.explanation: This arterial-phase attachment route represents a type I sealing failure. Prompt seal repair is appropriate even before the sac enlarges; the available healthy neck makes proximal extension a supported option.

questions.stem: Which next step should have been selected at {patientName}'s recorded assessment?

answerChoices.label: Urgent CT angiography during aortic-team preparation
Direct operating-room transfer for open aortic control
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Immediate control can be necessary in collapse, but the current serial observations support obtaining repair-planning CT first.

answerChoices.label: Further resuscitation before any cross-sectional planning
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The record already shows restored mentation and sustained pressure over repeated assessments; further normalizing physiology before defining the repair anatomy unnecessarily postpones the next supported step.

questions.explanation: Use the current serial perfusion observations, not the initial pressure in isolation. At this recorded point urgent CT can define rupture and repair anatomy while definitive aortic care is prepared. Persistent or renewed circulatory collapse would change that balance toward immediate aortic control.

questions.stem: Which definitive hospital plan should have been selected from {patientName}'s initial CTA?

answerChoices.label: Emergency open ascending aortic repair
Urgent descending thoracic endovascular repair
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Treating the distal tear as a type-B problem does not address the acute ascending involvement.

answerChoices.label: Intravenous esmolol with CT angiographic follow-up
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Impulse control is background stabilization but not definitive treatment of acute ascending dissection.

questions.explanation: Ascending involvement determines the type-A pathway even when the entry tear is distal. Stable current pressure does not remove the need for emergency surgical treatment of acute ascending dissection.

questions.stem: Which infusion change should have followed {patientName}'s recorded treatment response?

answerChoices.label: Add intravenous nicardipine infusion
Increase the intravenous esmolol infusion
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Escalating rate-slowing therapy does not best address the remaining pressure target once the recorded rate response is adequate and perfusion is preserved.

answerChoices.label: Replace esmolol with intravenous diltiazem
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The record does not demonstrate beta-blocker intolerance or a rate-control failure requiring substitution; it shows persisting pressure elevation after a rate response.

questions.explanation: Rate and pressure are separate treatment targets. The observed rate response is within the guideline range, while pressure remains elevated. Add an intravenous vasodilator after initial beta blockade rather than simply intensifying rate reduction or substituting another rate-control agent. Nicardipine provides additional blood-pressure reduction while beta blockade continues.

questions.stem: Which left-subclavian strategy should have accompanied {patientName}'s elective TEVAR plan?

answerChoices.label: Carotid-subclavian bypass before aortic coverage
Aortic coverage, then bypass if arm ischemia develops
answerChoices.distractorRationale: An arm-symptom trigger does not protect the LIMA-dependent coronary circulation during elective coverage.

answerChoices.label: Carotid-subclavian transposition before aortic coverage
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Transposition requires proximal subclavian clamping, which can interrupt the patent pedicled LIMA coronary inflow; bypass avoids that required interruption.

questions.explanation: Protect the pedicled LIMA coronary inflow before elective LSA coverage. Bypass avoids the proximal subclavian clamp required for transposition; waiting for arm ischemia also fails to protect this coronary-dependent territory.

questions.stem: Which immediate rescue plan should have been activated for {patientName}'s postoperative findings?

answerChoices.label: Vasopressor-supported perfusion with CSF-drainage rescue
Esmolol-based pressure reduction with intravenous analgesia
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Further pressure reduction would work against perfusion rescue in this new postoperative neurologic syndrome.

answerChoices.label: Heparin anticoagulation with urgent aortoiliac thrombectomy
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Warm feet and preserved pulses make aortoiliac occlusion a poorer explanation than spinal perfusion injury.

questions.explanation: Bilateral leg weakness after hypotension with preserved limb pulses raises concern for spinal-cord ischemia. Activate perfusion rescue and specialist CSF-drainage assessment; the new phase calls for restoring cord perfusion rather than intensifying impulse reduction.

questions.stem: Which aneurysm plan should have been selected for {patientName}'s right popliteal lesion?

answerChoices.label: Plan popliteal aneurysm repair with vascular surgery
Start anticoagulation with popliteal duplex follow-up
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This addresses thrombotic risk without removing the demonstrated aneurysmal source. The supported strategy includes repair assessment rather than relying on medication as the definitive plan.

answerChoices.label: Continue annual popliteal duplex surveillance
answerChoices.distractorRationale: The asymptomatic small-aneurysm policy does not address repeated embolic complications in this record.

questions.explanation: Digital occlusions with a thrombus-containing PAA support distal embolization even when pedal pulses remain palpable. The complication warrants vascular repair planning below the usual asymptomatic size boundary. This selects repair versus medication/surveillance; conduit assessment and anatomy determine the eventual open or endovascular technique.

questions.stem: Which additional aneurysm study should have been selected after review of {patientName}'s original acquisitions?

exhibit.caption: Constructed original acquisition and observation log
cells: Outer aortic contours traced; maximum 2.5 cm
Deep venous compression and Doppler sequences
Femoral and popliteal veins compressible with venous flow

answerChoices.label: Left popliteal arterial duplex ultrasound
Abdominal aortic duplex ultrasound
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This is an appropriate associated site but does not address the remaining arterial target after an adequate abdominal CTA.

answerChoices.label: Thoracic aortic CT angiography
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A thoracic study does not complete the specifically supported opposite-popliteal and abdominal-aortic associated survey.

questions.explanation: Screening associated with a PAA includes the opposite popliteal artery and abdominal aorta. The acquired left-leg study documents venous compression and flow; that reassuring result does not assess the contralateral arterial target. The abdominal CTA already supplies the aortic component of this survey.

questions.stem: Which investigation should have followed {patientName}'s unrevealing upper endoscopy during that admission?

answerChoices.label: Multiphase abdominal CT angiography
Push enteroscopy into the distal duodenum
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This is a genuine new mucosal target beyond the previous examination, but it does not replace cross-sectional evaluation of the prosthetic reconstruction and surrounding infection concern.

answerChoices.label: Tagged-red-cell gastrointestinal bleeding scintigraphy
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Localization of intermittent bleeding does not characterize the prosthetic/infectious interface that links the other observations.

questions.explanation: Prosthetic aortic history, unexplained bloodstream infection and bleeding raise a linked vascular concern. Cross-sectional assessment is appropriate even when a proximal mucosal examination is unrevealing. Distal enteroscopy offers a real new luminal target, but that target does not substitute for evaluating the reconstruction and extraluminal findings.

questions.stem: Which repair approach should have been preferred for {patientName}'s intact thoracoabdominal aneurysm?

answerChoices.label: Open thoracoabdominal graft replacement
Branched endovascular thoracoabdominal repair
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Technical feasibility does not erase the guideline preference for open repair in this heritable native-aorta setting.

answerChoices.label: Visceral debranching with thoracic endografting
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A hybrid operation still relies on endograft sealing in the diseased native aorta rather than providing the preferred open reconstruction.

questions.explanation: For an intact TAAA requiring repair in Marfan syndrome, the checked multisociety guideline favors open repair. Native-aortic tissue disease and long-term durability matter even when branched or hybrid reconstruction is technically possible.

authorChecks.cueAttack: Removed the conclusion that no abdominal imaging had ever occurred. The record now names a real acquisition endpoint that includes an upper abdominal segment. No label states whether that acquisition completed screening; all choices are concrete imaging plans.
authorChecks.stageAndCategory: Initial preventive imaging plans after review of an existing aortic acquisition.
reasoningSteps: Infer from the celiac-level endpoint that the infrarenal survey remains incomplete despite a CTA title.
Apply ever-smoker eligibility and the preventive care phase to choose ultrasound rather than a diagnostic CTA or no study.
authorChecks.difficulty: Fair moderate author prediction. Coverage interpretation now changes a credible no-imaging plan. A harder device or acute-care problem would change the established screening meaning; no foundational exception or measured difficulty is claimed.
authorChecks.decidingObservation: The archived acquisition ends near the celiac origin rather than extending through the infrarenal aorta.
authorChecks.closestError: No further imaging because an aortic CTA has already been performed.
authorChecks.consequence: Leaving the intended abdominal screening territory unassessed.
authorChecks.deletionTest: Without the caudal endpoint, completed prior screening cannot be decided. Age and smoking determine whether the incomplete survey matters. Removed the redundant never-imaged sentence.
authorChecks.counterfactual: Extend the prior adequately visualized acquisition through the infrarenal aorta and document normal dimensions: no additional one-time screen becomes the best offered plan.
authorChecks.sequenceReview: This v2 question is standalone. The PASS referral remains in its entire original v1 case with original earlier feedback; no new presentation or feedback is silently attached to that PASS.
authorChecks.repairAndRecheck: Applied the independent review's specific deletion and re-solved all three plans. Kept a moderate boundary rather than inventing an unrelated difficult criterion.

authorChecks.cueAttack: The neutral task no longer demands an imaging correction. A compact acquisition table supplies the actual planes and source-series adequacy; the key does not repeat a distinctive perpendicular phrase. Repair assessment and surveillance are genuine competing responses to the apparent change.
authorChecks.stageAndCategory: Next aortic management plan after discordant serial reports, before a growth claim is accepted.
reasoningSteps: Interpret the relationship between vessel curvature, measurement plane and reported change.
Decide whether to verify the change now, apply a growth-based repair policy or apply a size-based surveillance band.
authorChecks.difficulty: Moderate/hard prediction: both the apparent growth over six months and a subthreshold latest diameter invite defensible-looking but incompatible policies. Neither can be applied correctly until measurement validity is resolved.
authorChecks.decidingObservation: Different image planes despite adequate complete source volumes from both time points.
authorChecks.closestError: Repair referral based on the apparent six-month enlargement as if it were confirmed.
authorChecks.consequence: Escalating care on an invalid comparison or overlooking a consequential trajectory by merely rescheduling surveillance.
authorChecks.deletionTest: Removing the plane or source-volume rows changes the validity of the comparison. Removing the interval would make a growth-rate interpretation unfair; six months is now explicit.
authorChecks.counterfactual: Make both values matched orthogonal outer-wall measurements at the same landmark: the confirmed six-month increase supports the offered repair-evaluation plan.
authorChecks.sequenceReview: Later v2 nodes receive a reconciled comparison and a separate change in ultrasound adequacy, then a new pain episode. The explanation gives no later MRI or pain-attribution answer.
authorChecks.repairAndRecheck: Replaced the deliberately repeated bad CT protocol foil with actual growth-versus-surveillance decisions. Added only the directly checked ACC/AHA growth boundary; no new automatic operation rule.

authorChecks.cueAttack: Removed the supplied adequate-ultrasound conclusion and the three interval labels. The raw acoustic-window observations and immediate contrast reaction are necessary constraints; all options are named aortic investigations with their own wait metadata.
authorChecks.stageAndCategory: Complete a current nondiagnostic surveillance examination with an appropriate imaging modality.
reasoningSteps: Determine that the current examination cannot establish the full aneurysm dimension despite the prior stable comparison.
Select cross-sectional imaging while accounting for the serious prior iodinated-contrast response.
authorChecks.difficulty: Moderate/hard prediction: repeating the customary surveillance modality and automatically escalating to CTA are each credible errors. The new clinical meaning is modality adequacy, so the old interval concept/history is retained separately.
authorChecks.decidingObservation: The posterior sac boundary is not measurable on the current views, and the prior iodinated injection produced an immediate systemic reaction.
authorChecks.closestError: Order CTA after correctly recognizing that ultrasound is inadequate.
authorChecks.consequence: Unnecessary repeat exposure to the implicated contrast class, or failure to establish an interpretable aneurysm dimension.
authorChecks.deletionTest: Remove the contrast reaction and CT becomes a supported alternative; remove the acoustic limitation and ordinary ultrasound remains appropriate. The actual six-month interval eliminates the original rate-assessment ambiguity.
authorChecks.counterfactual: Provide complete reproducible current ultrasound visualization of the sac: duplex becomes the appropriate offered study despite the contrast history.
authorChecks.sequenceReview: The preceding measurement feedback does not teach MRI selection. The later pain record uses MR angiography, maintaining the contrast-history chronology rather than silently performing another routine iodinated CTA.
authorChecks.repairAndRecheck: Changed the scored meaning explicitly instead of claiming that a corrected diameter creates two new inferences. Verified ACC/AHA ultrasound/CT/MRI recommendations and retained the old meaning without FSRS transfer.

authorChecks.cueAttack: Removed 'should have replaced surveillance' from the task and the blanket claim excluding every alternative cause. The record instead gives a genuine competing lumbar observation, its chronology and the pain localization. Both alternative plans involve real assessment or follow-up.
authorChecks.stageAndCategory: Current inpatient aortic-versus-spine/observation plans after a new pain evaluation.
reasoningSteps: Use the pain behavior, focal examination and unchanged lumbar image to assess the competing attribution.
Apply that attribution to inpatient vascular repair assessment rather than the earlier asymptomatic size policy.
authorChecks.difficulty: Fair moderate prediction: an incidental spine abnormality and an intact aneurysm image are credible anchors. Diagnostic attribution remains a clinical judgment; the draft does not pretend that imaging alone proves the pain source.
authorChecks.decidingObservation: New persistent rest pain is reproduced over the aortic mass while the competing lumbar structural finding is unchanged.
authorChecks.closestError: Spine MRI first because a lumbar deformity appears in the imaging record.
authorChecks.consequence: Delaying aortic assessment after a meaningful change in symptoms.
authorChecks.deletionTest: Without the actual competing lumbar finding this is a simpler symptom-trigger rule. Without chronology and focal localization, choosing the vascular pathway would be less defensible. No blanket negative supplies the interpretation.
authorChecks.counterfactual: Replace aortic tenderness/rest pain with reproducible mechanical back pain and new corresponding spinal findings: the spine-directed investigation becomes reasonable before attributing symptoms to the AAA.
authorChecks.sequenceReview: Earlier feedback concerns imaging adequacy and does not rehearse pain as a repair indication. MR angiography preserves the serious iodinated-contrast history established in the preceding v2 node.
authorChecks.repairAndRecheck: Re-solved the neutral task after deleting the cue and broad exclusion. Kept the supported moderate attribution problem rather than adding an unsourced imaging sign or compulsory operation deadline.

authorChecks.cueAttack: The presentation no longer announces an established 5.1-cm aneurysm as a completed interpretation. The constructed table provides competing measured structures. All labels are concrete management plans with comparable grammar; no mandatory-operation or generic shared-decision key is used.
authorChecks.stageAndCategory: Elective aortic management after a measurement record, before selecting any repair technique.
reasoningSteps: Identify the maximum full sac dimension rather than the residual flow channel.
Apply the female assessment boundary rather than the male threshold or the female interval for a smaller sac.
authorChecks.difficulty: Moderate prediction: each surveillance choice follows a different credible error, so the learner must resolve both dimension and population. It is not claimed to be a universal mandatory operation rule.
authorChecks.decidingObservation: A 5.1-cm outer contour surrounds a smaller flowing channel in a woman.
authorChecks.closestError: Use the full size but apply a male threshold and defer assessment for six months.
authorChecks.consequence: Postponing repair assessment or following the wrong sac-size band.
authorChecks.deletionTest: Removing the contour/channel distinction leaves only threshold recall; removing sex makes the assessment-versus-six-month choice different. Extra fitness statements were not added to manufacture difficulty.

Apply its pressure-risk significance rather than letting stable sac size determine observation.

authorChecks.stageAndCategory: Immediate hospital next-step plans after a painful large AAA is detected, before definitive repair anatomy is known.

Choose urgent planning imaging versus direct control or further stabilization at this actual time point.

Apply the ascending extent to immediate operative management despite stable physiology.

authorChecks.sequenceReview: Standalone; no other dissection case's feedback is assumed visible. No new ICU setting, bedside treatment execution or live consultation is required.

authorChecks.cueAttack: The former unique conditional medical option versus two operations is gone. All choices are named infusion changes. Safety and treatment-response observations apply to all competing pharmacologic strategies rather than appearing as a beta-blocker permission list.
authorChecks.stageAndCategory: Next infusion change after initial monitored beta blockade, not whether every descending dissection requires an operation.
reasoningSteps: Interpret the discordant treatment response: rate has responded, pressure has not, with current perfusion preserved.
Select added vasodilation rather than further rate reduction or rate-agent substitution.

Choose pre-coverage inflow preservation that avoids the proximal clamp required for transposition, rather than waiting for arm symptoms.

Apply that durability boundary and current operability to the approach preference.

explanation.text: The celiac-level endpoint leaves the infrarenal aorta unexamined. Apply the screening recommendation to the actual coverage, not the examination's title: abdominal ultrasound is the initial preventive screen for this eligible former smoker.

choices.label: Obtain abdominal aortic ultrasound
choices.rationale: The prior acquisition stops above the infrarenal aorta. His age and former smoking history still support an abdominal screen.
choices.temptation: Recognizes that part of the abdominal aorta on a chest scan is not a completed infrarenal survey.
choices.counterfactual: A prior adequate abdominal acquisition documenting the full infrarenal aorta would support no additional one-time screen.

choices.label: Obtain abdominal aortic CT angiography
choices.rationale: His record requires a first preventive abdominal screen, not detailed repair or acute-symptom anatomy; ultrasound is the supported initial modality.
choices.temptation: Extends the prior CTA technique to the unexamined lower segment because it offers more detail.
choices.counterfactual: New aneurysm-attributable symptoms would change the task to diagnostic cross-sectional imaging.

choices.label: Arrange no additional aortic imaging
choices.rationale: The study's caudal endpoint leaves the infrarenal aorta outside the acquisition. Smoking cessation does not negate the ever-smoker screening indication.
choices.temptation: Counts a study labeled aortic CTA as covering the entire aorta.
choices.counterfactual: A documented adequate full infrarenal study could make another screening examination unnecessary.

explanation.text: The reported 0.7-cm difference spans different measurement planes. Use the adequate acquired volumes to establish a matched comparison before interpreting growth. Confirmed enlargement of that amount over six months could change repair assessment, so the discrepancy should not simply be deferred to routine surveillance.

choices.label: Reconstruct the serial CT volumes for matched measurements
choices.rationale: The apparent increase uses different planes. Adequate source volumes permit a valid comparison before using enlargement to determine repair assessment.
choices.temptation: Separates a changed number from established biological growth.
choices.counterfactual: Comparable orthogonal measurements confirming the same change over six months could support vascular repair evaluation.

choices.label: Refer for repair evaluation based on serial enlargement
choices.rationale: The amount and interval would matter if the measurements were comparable, but the plane discrepancy prevents treating the reported difference as confirmed growth.
choices.temptation: Correctly recognizes a potentially important rate but assumes the two report values are interchangeable.
choices.counterfactual: A confirmed increase from 4.6 to 5.3 cm using the same reproducible method over six months makes repair evaluation reasonable.

choices.label: Schedule ultrasound follow-up using the latest reported size
choices.rationale: Applying a surveillance band to the unreconciled latest value does not resolve whether a consequential interval change occurred.
choices.temptation: Uses the current diameter band while overlooking a potentially important but unvalidated trajectory.
choices.counterfactual: Once comparable imaging establishes a stable unrepaired male AAA near the repair threshold, six-month ultrasound may be appropriate.

explanation.text: Current ultrasound adequacy matters more than the fact that ultrasound was useful previously. Cross-sectional assessment is needed when the sac is not defined, and MRI is reasonable when CT is contraindicated. The earlier matched measurements do not establish the current sac size after an inadequate examination.

choices.label: MRI of the abdominal aorta
choices.rationale: The current ultrasound does not define full sac size; MRI provides cross-sectional assessment without requiring the iodinated-contrast exposure implicated in his prior reaction.
choices.temptation: Uses current test adequacy and the actual previous contrast response rather than reusing a formerly adequate modality.
choices.counterfactual: If the full sac were visualized reproducibly on the current ultrasound, ultrasound surveillance would remain appropriate.

choices.label: CT angiography of the abdominal aorta
choices.rationale: Cross-sectional imaging addresses the inadequate ultrasound, but this proposed contrast examination disregards the serious prior immediate reaction when MRI is a supported alternative.
choices.temptation: Correctly escalates imaging after an incomplete study but ignores the acquisition-specific constraint.
choices.counterfactual: Without an important CT contraindication, CT is a supported way to define an inadequately visualized AAA.

choices.label: Duplex ultrasound of the abdominal aorta
choices.rationale: The prior success of ultrasound does not establish a usable current outer-wall measurement through the documented acoustic limitation.
choices.temptation: Applies the ordinary small-AAA modality without checking whether this examination can actually measure the sac.
choices.counterfactual: An adequate current acoustic window and complete outer-wall visualization support ultrasound follow-up.

explanation.text: The pain pattern and focal tenderness make the aneurysm clinically concerning even though MR imaging shows no extravasation. The unchanged lumbar finding does not by itself explain this new syndrome. Inpatient vascular repair assessment is appropriate; a size-based asymptomatic surveillance rule does not settle this admission.

choices.label: Inpatient vascular assessment for aneurysm repair
choices.rationale: New focal aortic tenderness and persistent nonmechanical pain change the previously asymptomatic premise despite an intact image and smaller diameter.
choices.temptation: Interprets current symptom localization rather than treating an intact sac as necessarily asymptomatic.
choices.counterfactual: A demonstrated nonaneurysmal mechanical pain syndrome with no aortic tenderness could support a spine-directed plan and aneurysm surveillance.

choices.label: Inpatient lumbar MRI before vascular assessment
choices.rationale: The unchanged structural spine finding does not establish that it explains the new rest pain and focal pain reproduced over the aorta.
choices.temptation: Anchors on a visible spinal abnormality and delays the aortic assessment.
choices.counterfactual: New focal mechanical or neurologic findings corresponding to a new spinal lesion would strengthen a spine-directed investigation.

choices.label: Clinical observation with scheduled aortic ultrasound follow-up
choices.rationale: Routine observation and surveillance do not address the new aneurysm-localized symptoms simply because the scan shows no leak.
choices.temptation: Continues the prior small-AAA policy after interpreting intact imaging as reassurance.
choices.counterfactual: If the pain resolved with a clearly supported separate cause and aortic symptoms were absent, size-based follow-up could again be appropriate.

explanation.text: Use the maximum outer-wall sac dimension. ACC/AHA recommends repair at the female size boundary, while SVS frames repair in the 5.0-5.4-cm range as a suggestion; both support specialist repair assessment in this supplied context. Neither diameter nor sex selects a procedure or removes the need to consider operative risk and patient goals.

choices.label: Arrange elective vascular repair assessment
choices.rationale: The full outer contour, not the flowing channel, reaches the female repair-assessment range. This supports evaluation rather than choosing an operation automatically.
choices.temptation: Integrates which dimension matters with the population-specific recommendation.
choices.counterfactual: A smaller full sac could instead support continued surveillance.

choices.label: Arrange aortic ultrasound in six months
choices.rationale: This can follow a male threshold applied to the full sac or a surveillance-only policy, but it postpones the supported female repair assessment here.
choices.temptation: Uses the familiar male boundary despite correctly reading the outer dimension.
choices.counterfactual: For an asymptomatic man with the same 5.1-cm full sac, six-month surveillance can be appropriate.

choices.label: Arrange aortic ultrasound in twelve months
choices.rationale: The 4.2-cm flowing channel is not the aneurysm's full dimension used for the female surveillance band.
choices.temptation: Applies the correct female interval to the wrong measured structure.
choices.counterfactual: An asymptomatic woman whose full sac, rather than flowing channel, measures 4.2 cm could have annual ultrasound.

explanation.text: The current imaging leaves the right internal iliac as the remaining direct pelvic inflow. Preserve that route as part of exclusion planning when feasible. This is a strategy decision: the scan does not by itself establish eligibility for a particular iliac branch device, and the final preserving reconstruction requires separate anatomic planning.

choices.label: Preserve right internal-iliac inflow during bilateral external-iliac extension
choices.rationale: The right internal iliac is the remaining direct pelvic inflow. An exclusion strategy should preserve it when feasible rather than intentionally eliminating that route.
choices.temptation: Maps the opacified vessel and planned exclusion to the remaining pelvic supply.
choices.counterfactual: If the right side were occluded and the left internal iliac supplied the pelvis, left-sided preservation would be the relevant goal.

choices.label: Preserve left internal-iliac inflow during bilateral external-iliac extension
choices.rationale: The left channel is already occluded; assigning preservation to that side does not protect the patent right pelvic supply from the planned coverage.
choices.temptation: Reverses the side or counts a formerly named artery as current patent inflow.
choices.counterfactual: A patent left internal iliac with an occluded right side would make left-sided preservation the appropriate goal.

choices.label: Exclude both internal-iliac origins during bilateral external-iliac extension
choices.rationale: This would intentionally interrupt the remaining right-sided route instead of preserving at least one direct hypogastric inflow when feasible.
choices.temptation: Prioritizes a simple distal exclusion configuration and relies on unspecified collateral compensation.
choices.counterfactual: When both direct routes are already lost or preserving inflow is truly infeasible, the clinical team must consider a different risk/strategy balance rather than assuming this draft's preserving reconstruction.

explanation.text: Delayed branch-associated flow with an unchanged sac supports continued surveillance. A visible leak is not enough to choose its treatment; source and sac behavior matter.

choices.label: Continue aortic duplex imaging surveillance
choices.rationale: The branch origin and unchanged sac support observation with continued imaging.
choices.temptation: Interprets both the leak route and sac behavior.
choices.counterfactual: A direct attachment leak or a growing sac would require a different evaluation or intervention.

choices.label: Embolize the lumbar inflow and sac cavity
choices.rationale: A visible branch leak does not by itself establish a treatment benefit when the sac is stable.
choices.temptation: Treats persistence of any contrast outside the graft as a repair indication.
choices.counterfactual: A persistent proven branch leak with consequential sac growth can merit embolization after other sources are excluded.

choices.label: Extend the proximal seal with an aortic cuff
choices.rationale: The observed inflow is from lumbar branches, not the proximal attachment.
choices.temptation: Confuses every leak with a proximal seal failure.
choices.counterfactual: A proximal attachment leak with a usable extra landing segment would favor cuff extension.

explanation.text: Do not carry forward a branch-leak label when a growing sac has an uncertain current inflow source. Problem-solving aortography can assess the attachments and modular junctions before choosing a branch-directed treatment.

choices.label: Aortography across the seal zones and graft junctions
choices.rationale: The enlarging sac and uncertain source require reassessment for direct graft or attachment inflow before targeting a branch.
choices.temptation: Questions whether the old branch label explains the current growth.
choices.counterfactual: A clearly established enlarging isolated branch leak could move directly to targeted branch mapping and embolization.

choices.label: Selective mesenteric-to-inferior-mesenteric collateral angiography
choices.rationale: This maps a branch route but does not resolve the possible attachment or component defect producing the current sac growth.
choices.temptation: Extends the previous type-II attribution to a new scan without validating it.
choices.counterfactual: Proven inferior-mesenteric branch inflow into a growing sac can justify this approach.

choices.label: Selective iliolumbar-to-lumbar collateral angiography
choices.rationale: The lumbar branch near the contrast focus does not establish that it is the only source.
choices.temptation: Anchors on the branch seen on the earlier surveillance images.
choices.counterfactual: A confirmed isolated lumbar leak with sac growth can be mapped for targeted embolization.

explanation.text: The problem is loss of covered continuity, not simply insufficient expansion. A covered bridge can close a separated modular junction. Balloon remodelling or bare-metal reinforcement addresses other apposition/support problems but does not itself cover a fabric gap.

choices.label: Covered stent-graft bridging at the modular junction
choices.rationale: A fabric gap provides a direct route into the sac. A covered bridge restores the missing barrier between the aligned components.
choices.temptation: Uses the observed mechanical defect to select a repair that actually excludes the channel.
choices.counterfactual: If the components still overlapped and the problem were remediable incomplete expansion, balloon remodelling could be appropriate.

choices.label: Balloon remodelling at the modular junction
choices.rationale: Expansion can improve apposition where fabric overlaps, but cannot supply the absent covering between separated ends.
choices.temptation: Treats every junctional leak as incomplete expansion of an existing overlap.
choices.counterfactual: An intraoperative leak from incomplete expansion within a maintained overlap can be treated by balloon remodelling.

choices.label: Bare-metal stent reinforcement at the leaking segment
choices.rationale: Radial scaffolding does not add a covering across the demonstrated open channel to the sac.
choices.temptation: Confuses mechanical support with reconstruction of the exclusion barrier.
choices.counterfactual: Selected attachment-apposition leaks can use bare-metal reinforcement as an adjunct when the covered fabric and sealing anatomy are present.

explanation.text: This arterial-phase attachment route represents a type I sealing failure. Prompt seal repair is appropriate even before the sac enlarges; the available healthy neck makes proximal extension a supported option.

choices.label: Extend the proximal seal with an aortic cuff
choices.rationale: Direct attachment inflow requires prompt seal correction; the remaining healthy segment supports a cuff.
choices.temptation: Distinguishes a sealing defect from a stable branch leak.
choices.counterfactual: Absent a usable neck, a more complex reconstruction would need consideration.

choices.label: Continue aortic duplex imaging surveillance
choices.rationale: Stable sac size does not justify observation of an established late direct attachment leak.
choices.temptation: Overgeneralizes conservative care for stable type-II flow.
choices.counterfactual: A confirmed isolated branch leak with stable sac size supports surveillance.

choices.label: Embolize the lumbar inflow and sac cavity
choices.rationale: The demonstrated source is the proximal attachment, not a side branch.
choices.temptation: Treats contrast in the sac as a branch-leak problem regardless of its observed source.
choices.counterfactual: A growing isolated branch leak could support branch/sac embolization.

explanation.text: Use the current serial perfusion observations, not the initial pressure in isolation. At this recorded point urgent CT can define rupture and repair anatomy while definitive aortic care is prepared. Persistent or renewed circulatory collapse would change that balance toward immediate aortic control.

choices.label: Urgent CT angiography during aortic-team preparation
choices.rationale: Repeated preserved pressure and mentation after initial resuscitation support urgent cross-sectional repair planning rather than another detection-only examination.
choices.temptation: Uses the current trajectory instead of classifying the patient solely from the first low reading.
choices.counterfactual: A renewed collapse or inability to sustain perfusion would make a direct hemorrhage-control pathway appropriate instead.

choices.label: Direct operating-room transfer for open aortic control
choices.rationale: Immediate control can be necessary in collapse, but the current serial observations support obtaining repair-planning CT first.
choices.temptation: Treats an initially low pressure and large aneurysm as proof that planning imaging is no longer possible.
choices.counterfactual: Persistent deterioration in circulation despite initial resuscitation would favor proceeding to hemorrhage control rather than delaying for CT.

choices.label: Further resuscitation before any cross-sectional planning
choices.rationale: The record already shows restored mentation and sustained pressure over repeated assessments; further normalizing physiology before defining the repair anatomy unnecessarily postpones the next supported step.
choices.temptation: Waits for entirely normal vital signs rather than judging whether current perfusion permits urgent planning.
choices.counterfactual: If perfusion remained inadequate for safe movement to CT, immediate resuscitation alongside a hemorrhage-control plan would be necessary.

explanation.text: Ascending involvement determines the type-A pathway even when the entry tear is distal. Stable current pressure does not remove the need for emergency surgical treatment of acute ascending dissection.

choices.label: Emergency open ascending aortic repair
choices.rationale: Ascending involvement places this in the type-A pathway despite a descending entry tear.
choices.temptation: Classifies by the involved segment and applies its urgent surgical consequence.
choices.counterfactual: A flap confined distal to the left subclavian without complications would favor initial medical treatment.

choices.label: Urgent descending thoracic endovascular repair
choices.rationale: Treating the distal tear as a type-B problem does not address the acute ascending involvement.
choices.temptation: Classifies the dissection by the tear location alone.
choices.counterfactual: A complicated dissection confined to the descending aorta with suitable anatomy can favor TEVAR.

choices.label: Intravenous esmolol with CT angiographic follow-up
choices.rationale: Impulse control is background stabilization but not definitive treatment of acute ascending dissection.
choices.temptation: Uses normotension and absence of malperfusion to choose an uncomplicated type-B pathway.
choices.counterfactual: An uncomplicated dissection confined to the descending aorta initially receives medical therapy and monitoring.

explanation.text: Rate and pressure are separate treatment targets. The observed rate response is within the guideline range, while pressure remains elevated. Add an intravenous vasodilator after initial beta blockade rather than simply intensifying rate reduction or substituting another rate-control agent. Nicardipine provides additional blood-pressure reduction while beta blockade continues.

choices.label: Add intravenous nicardipine infusion
choices.rationale: Rate has entered the guideline target range while pressure remains uncontrolled; added vasodilation addresses the remaining treatment target after beta blockade.
choices.temptation: Separates the achieved chronotropic response from the persisting pressure problem.
choices.counterfactual: If heart rate remained markedly elevated before adequate beta blockade, further beta-blocker titration could precede vasodilation.

choices.label: Increase the intravenous esmolol infusion
choices.rationale: Escalating rate-slowing therapy does not best address the remaining pressure target once the recorded rate response is adequate and perfusion is preserved.
choices.temptation: Uses one infusion to pursue both goals without interpreting which goal has already responded.
choices.counterfactual: Persisting sinus tachycardia with tolerable perfusion and no limiting response could support further beta-blocker titration.

choices.label: Replace esmolol with intravenous diltiazem
choices.rationale: The record does not demonstrate beta-blocker intolerance or a rate-control failure requiring substitution; it shows persisting pressure elevation after a rate response.
choices.temptation: Treats incomplete pressure response as failure of the chosen rate-control drug class.
choices.counterfactual: A genuine beta-blocker contraindication or intolerance can favor a nondihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker for rate control.

explanation.text: Protect the pedicled LIMA coronary inflow before elective LSA coverage. Bypass avoids the proximal subclavian clamp required for transposition; waiting for arm ischemia also fails to protect this coronary-dependent territory.

choices.label: Carotid-subclavian bypass before aortic coverage
choices.rationale: LSA interruption threatens inflow to the patent LIMA graft supplying an occluded native LAD territory.
choices.temptation: Follows the coronary conduit back to its inflow origin.
choices.counterfactual: If no LSA-dependent coronary or other critical inflow existed, timing and need could differ, particularly in an emergency.

choices.label: Aortic coverage, then bypass if arm ischemia develops
choices.rationale: An arm-symptom trigger does not protect the LIMA-dependent coronary circulation during elective coverage.
choices.temptation: Treats upper-extremity symptoms as the only meaningful consequence of LSA interruption.
choices.counterfactual: Selective delayed revascularization may fit some emergency coverings without critical LSA-dependent inflow.

choices.label: Carotid-subclavian transposition before aortic coverage
choices.rationale: Transposition requires proximal subclavian clamping, which can interrupt the patent pedicled LIMA coronary inflow; bypass avoids that required interruption.
choices.temptation: Chooses a durable LSA revascularization while overlooking its proximal clamp sequence.
choices.counterfactual: Without a patent pedicled LIMA or another clamp-dependent inflow, transposition can be a reasonable LSA revascularization technique.

explanation.text: Bilateral leg weakness after hypotension with preserved limb pulses raises concern for spinal-cord ischemia. Activate perfusion rescue and specialist CSF-drainage assessment; the new phase calls for restoring cord perfusion rather than intensifying impulse reduction.

choices.label: Vasopressor-supported perfusion with CSF-drainage rescue
choices.rationale: The pattern points to spinal-cord perfusion injury; pressure support and reduction of intrathecal pressure address that mechanism.
choices.temptation: Links bilateral motor findings with the hypotensive trigger and preserved limb inflow.
choices.counterfactual: A focal cerebral syndrome or arterial inflow loss would require a different rescue target.

choices.label: Esmolol-based pressure reduction with intravenous analgesia
choices.rationale: Further pressure reduction would work against perfusion rescue in this new postoperative neurologic syndrome.
choices.temptation: Carries an acute aortic impulse-reduction plan into a phase where low pressure is the precipitating problem.
choices.counterfactual: An unrepaired hypertensive acute aortic syndrome without cord hypoperfusion supports impulse control.

choices.label: Heparin anticoagulation with urgent aortoiliac thrombectomy
choices.rationale: Warm feet and preserved pulses make aortoiliac occlusion a poorer explanation than spinal perfusion injury.
choices.temptation: Interprets leg weakness after endovascular repair as an access or limb-occlusion complication.
choices.counterfactual: Sudden cold pulseless legs with demonstrated aortoiliac occlusion could require this pathway.

explanation.text: Digital occlusions with a thrombus-containing PAA support distal embolization even when pedal pulses remain palpable. The complication warrants vascular repair planning below the usual asymptomatic size boundary. This selects repair versus medication/surveillance; conduit assessment and anatomy determine the eventual open or endovascular technique.

choices.label: Plan popliteal aneurysm repair with vascular surgery
choices.rationale: Repeated digital embolic findings and mural thrombus support aneurysm source repair consideration despite a diameter below 20 mm.
choices.temptation: Uses the complication rather than size alone to choose the treatment strategy.
choices.counterfactual: A small asymptomatic lesion without thrombus or embolic findings can instead undergo surveillance.

choices.label: Start anticoagulation with popliteal duplex follow-up
choices.rationale: This addresses thrombotic risk without removing the demonstrated aneurysmal source. The supported strategy includes repair assessment rather than relying on medication as the definitive plan.
choices.temptation: Treats the embolic consequence without changing the persisting source.
choices.counterfactual: Prohibitive repair risk or an unavoidable treatment delay may require an interim specialist-directed medical strategy.

choices.label: Continue annual popliteal duplex surveillance
choices.rationale: The asymptomatic small-aneurysm policy does not address repeated embolic complications in this record.
choices.temptation: Lets the 18-mm diameter and palpable pedal pulses override the digital arterial findings.
choices.counterfactual: A small stable asymptomatic PAA without thrombus/embolism can be monitored.

explanation.text: Screening associated with a PAA includes the opposite popliteal artery and abdominal aorta. The acquired left-leg study documents venous compression and flow; that reassuring result does not assess the contralateral arterial target. The abdominal CTA already supplies the aortic component of this survey.

choices.label: Left popliteal arterial duplex ultrasound
choices.rationale: The left-leg examination evaluates veins, not a contralateral arterial aneurysm; the abdominal aorta is already adequately depicted.
choices.temptation: Separates a reassuring examination at the wrong vascular target from the associated arterial survey still needed.
choices.counterfactual: An adequate left arterial examination with an unassessed abdominal aorta would instead support abdominal aortic screening.

choices.label: Abdominal aortic duplex ultrasound
choices.rationale: This is an appropriate associated site but does not address the remaining arterial target after an adequate abdominal CTA.
choices.temptation: Recalls the AAA association while mistaking the left venous examination for a completed left arterial survey.
choices.counterfactual: An abdominal acquisition that omitted the infrarenal aorta would make a dedicated aortic study appropriate.

choices.label: Thoracic aortic CT angiography
choices.rationale: A thoracic study does not complete the specifically supported opposite-popliteal and abdominal-aortic associated survey.
choices.temptation: Generalizes aneurysm association to another arterial territory while treating the recorded left-leg study as sufficient.
choices.counterfactual: An independent thoracic or heritable-aortopathy indication can justify thoracic imaging.

explanation.text: Prosthetic aortic history, unexplained bloodstream infection and bleeding raise a linked vascular concern. Cross-sectional assessment is appropriate even when a proximal mucosal examination is unrevealing. Distal enteroscopy offers a real new luminal target, but that target does not substitute for evaluating the reconstruction and extraluminal findings.

choices.label: Multiphase abdominal CT angiography
choices.rationale: The combination of prosthetic aortic history, unexplained bacteremia and bleeding calls for cross-sectional vascular and extraluminal assessment.
choices.temptation: Interprets the infection/bleeding link before choosing the test's acquisition scope.
choices.counterfactual: A clearly localized mucosal source without graft-related concern could instead favor directed endoscopic evaluation.

choices.label: Push enteroscopy into the distal duodenum
choices.rationale: This is a genuine new mucosal target beyond the previous examination, but it does not replace cross-sectional evaluation of the prosthetic reconstruction and surrounding infection concern.
choices.temptation: Correctly recognizes the prior endoscopy's limited reach but treats the remaining problem as mucosal bleeding alone.
choices.counterfactual: Persistent bleeding localized to a distal-duodenal mucosal lesion without an unresolved prosthetic-infection concern could support this investigation.

choices.label: Tagged-red-cell gastrointestinal bleeding scintigraphy
choices.rationale: Localization of intermittent bleeding does not characterize the prosthetic/infectious interface that links the other observations.
choices.temptation: Selects a bleeding-localization pathway without integrating the persistent bloodstream findings and aortic history.
choices.counterfactual: Intermittent bleeding with graft pathology adequately excluded may require a separate localization pathway.

explanation.text: For an intact TAAA requiring repair in Marfan syndrome, the checked multisociety guideline favors open repair. Native-aortic tissue disease and long-term durability matter even when branched or hybrid reconstruction is technically possible.

choices.label: Open thoracoabdominal graft replacement
choices.rationale: Heritable native-aorta disease in an operable patient favors open reconstruction when repair is required.
choices.temptation: Distinguishes the tissue disease from an ordinary degenerative aneurysm.
choices.counterfactual: Severe operative prohibitions or emergency bridging needs can change the balance.

choices.label: Branched endovascular thoracoabdominal repair
choices.rationale: Technical feasibility does not erase the guideline preference for open repair in this heritable native-aorta setting.
choices.temptation: Generalizes the lower initial invasiveness of endovascular repair to all aneurysm substrates.
choices.counterfactual: An appropriate degenerative TAAA patient with higher open risk may be considered for branched repair.

choices.label: Visceral debranching with thoracic endografting
choices.rationale: A hybrid operation still relies on endograft sealing in the diseased native aorta rather than providing the preferred open reconstruction.
choices.temptation: Assumes adding open visceral bypasses resolves the native-seal concern.
choices.counterfactual: Selected patients unsuitable for conventional open repair can require alternative hybrid strategies.

record.title: Distal entry tear with ascending extension
fairness: The distal entry and ascending extension create a real classification trap. The learner must classify by involved aorta and choose the corresponding emergency pathway despite preserved pressure.

The medical option is not an equivalent definitive plan for the supplied acute ascending involvement. Interim impulse therapy remains compatible with arranging surgery and is not negated by this task.
No confident clinical inaccuracy or nonmedical option-selection shortcut identified.
suggestions: Keep the distinction between entry location and ascending involvement. The word 'founder' is unnecessary framing but does not change the answer; a plain reference to reviewing the admission CTA would be cleaner.

record.title: Identifying the missing associated-aneurysm study
fairness: Left popliteal arterial duplex is the best offered additional study. The resident must identify the usual associated arterial screening targets, then distinguish a venous examination of the opposite leg from adequate arterial assessment and account for the existing aortic measurements.

Abdominal ultrasound is a credible failure to recognize the existing infrarenal aortic assessment. Thoracic CTA is a plausible overextension of aortic screening. The options are named investigations, and the exhibit does not label the left arterial survey as missing or inadequate.

The word left appears in both the record and answer, but only knowing that compressible veins do not assess a popliteal arterial aneurysm makes that match useful. I do not regard this necessary anatomic information as an unfair lexical cue.

The update explicitly remains in the same workup. The shared presentation establishes the right popliteal lesion and the table repeats its findings; no prior key is needed. The preceding explanation discusses embolization and repair without revealing survey targets. Associated PAA and AAA screening is high yield.

The recorded CTA coverage establishes the infrarenal aortic findings supplied here, not an examination of every abdominal or thoracic aortic segment. The explanation should keep its adequacy claim tied to the screening target; no confident reason to select a different offered study is identified.
suggestions: Consider trimming the generic sentence announcing that the file contains studies; the table already conveys that information. Keep the acquisition coverage and venous-versus-arterial observations.

record.title: Selecting the relevant AAA diameter and repair assessment
fairness: Elective vascular repair assessment is the best offered plan. The resident must select maximum outer-wall diameter rather than flowing-channel diameter, then apply a sex-specific repair-assessment decision in a patient without a supplied major competing life-limiting illness.

The exhibit is consequential: selecting the smaller channel measurement plausibly directs the learner toward surveillance. The interval choices are credible neighboring plans. The correct answer is not uniquely long or qualified, and there is no key-only verbal match.

The explanation appropriately distinguishes a repair recommendation from a suggestion across guidelines and asks for assessment rather than asserting automatic surgery or selecting a procedure from sex alone. I have not independently reverified the exact guideline boundaries offline; no confident contradiction is identified.

The subsequent planning CTA is a clearly later record and adds the iliac anatomy needed for its separate task. This first node does not teach which side must be preserved. AAA measurement and repair selection are high yield.

record.title: Unexplained bleeding and bacteremia after aortic grafting
fairness: Multiphase abdominal CTA is the best offered investigation. The resident must link prosthetic aortic surgery, recurrent bacteremia and intermittent GI bleeding, then choose evaluation of the reconstruction and extraluminal tissues despite an unrevealing proximal endoscopic examination.

Push enteroscopy is a credible competing new examination because the previous study did not inspect the distal duodenum. Tagged-red-cell scintigraphy is a credible attempt to localize intermittent bleeding. Neither replaces evaluation of the suspected graft-related process.

The known limit of upper-endoscopy coverage is explicitly supplied without claiming that the whole duodenum was normal. Preserved pressure between episodes makes this an imaging-selection question rather than an unacknowledged immediate-control emergency. No confident clinical inaccuracy is identified.

All labels name investigations at the same stage and no pre-answer diagnosis label or unique wording match names CTA. The standalone chronology is clear, and the stem identifies the preceding test and hospital decision. Secondary aortoenteric fistula or graft infection in this setting is high yield.

record.title: Definitive treatment of infected graft-enteric communication
fairness: The learner must interpret persistent infection plus a graft-to-bowel channel and distinguish definitive source control from hemorrhage bridging or suppressive therapy.

Graft removal with vascular and bowel reconstruction is the defensible best offered definitive strategy in the stated operable patient. The alternatives can have roles in other settings, which makes stability and operability necessary information rather than gratuitous permission.

The update follows imaging coherently and contains enough current information to answer independently. Earlier feedback identifies concern for a complication but does not prescribe this definitive operation.

fairness: The meaningful decision is to question the earlier branch-leak attribution when a larger sac and indeterminate graft-junction flow appear, then investigate a potential direct graft-related source before selective branch treatment.

The three choices are angiographic assessments at the same stage. Aortography is a defensible first offered assessment; selective collateral studies might subsequently be needed but do not replace assessment of the uncertain graft interface.

The update supplies the current uncertainty even if earlier feedback is not recalled. Prior advice that source and sac behavior matter is general scaffolding, not disclosure of this selected assessment.

record.title: Preserving pedicled LIMA inflow during elective TEVAR

authorGate.cueAttack: The complaint names the organ, not the modality. Chest CTA is retained because its inferior coverage boundary changes whether screening is complete. Three imaging plans use similar scope; both offered tests have wait metadata.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Initial preventive abdominal-aortic imaging plans; no repair or rupture action competes at this stage.
reasoningSteps: Infer that the infrarenal aorta was not assessed by the prior chest acquisition.
Apply age and ever-smoking eligibility to choose ultrasound rather than repeat chest work or diagnostic CTA.
authorGate.difficulty: Moderate prediction: an otherwise prepared PGY-2/3 may mistake remote cessation or prior thoracic CTA for completed screening. The ultrasound-versus-CTA distinction remains a narrower rule than the later complications.
authorGate.decidingObservation: The prior acquisition stops at the diaphragm and he has never had abdominal imaging.
authorGate.closestError: No additional imaging because an aortic CTA already exists.
authorGate.consequence: Missing an indicated abdominal-aortic screen.
authorGate.deletionTest: Removing prior-coverage information leaves uncertainty about a completed screen. Removing smoking or age changes eligibility. The number of pack-years is a fictional exposure, not an eligibility cutoff.
authorGate.counterfactual: Replace the chest study with a documented completed adequate abdominal aortic screen: no additional one-time screen becomes the best offered plan.
authorGate.sequenceReview: The first explanation gives no repair diameter or subsequent result. The later ultrasound appears only after this answer as a separate outside record; no test is executed in clinic.

authorGate.stageAndCategory: Initial preventive imaging plans after review of an existing aortic acquisition.
reasoningSteps: Infer from the celiac-level endpoint that the infrarenal survey remains incomplete despite a CTA title.
Apply ever-smoker eligibility and the preventive care phase to choose ultrasound rather than a diagnostic CTA or no study.
authorGate.difficulty: Fair moderate author prediction. Coverage interpretation now changes a credible no-imaging plan. A harder device or acute-care problem would change the established screening meaning; no foundational exception or measured difficulty is claimed.
authorGate.decidingObservation: The archived acquisition ends near the celiac origin rather than extending through the infrarenal aorta.
authorGate.closestError: No further imaging because an aortic CTA has already been performed.
authorGate.consequence: Leaving the intended abdominal screening territory unassessed.
authorGate.deletionTest: Without the caudal endpoint, completed prior screening cannot be decided. Age and smoking determine whether the incomplete survey matters. Removed the redundant never-imaged sentence.
authorGate.counterfactual: Extend the prior adequately visualized acquisition through the infrarenal aorta and document normal dimensions: no additional one-time screen becomes the best offered plan.
authorGate.sequenceReview: This v2 question is standalone. The PASS referral remains in its entire original v1 case with original earlier feedback; no new presentation or feedback is silently attached to that PASS.
authorGate.repairAndRecheck: Applied the independent review's specific deletion and re-solved all three plans. Kept a moderate boundary rather than inventing an unrelated difficult criterion.

explanation.text: The celiac-level endpoint leaves the infrarenal aorta unexamined. Apply the screening recommendation to the actual coverage, not the examination's title: abdominal ultrasound is the initial preventive screen for this eligible former smoker.

choices.label: Obtain abdominal aortic ultrasound
choices.rationale: The prior acquisition stops above the infrarenal aorta. His age and former smoking history still support an abdominal screen.
choices.temptation: Recognizes that part of the abdominal aorta on a chest scan is not a completed infrarenal survey.
choices.counterfactual: A prior adequate abdominal acquisition documenting the full infrarenal aorta would support no additional one-time screen.

choices.label: Obtain abdominal aortic CT angiography
choices.rationale: His record requires a first preventive abdominal screen, not detailed repair or acute-symptom anatomy; ultrasound is the supported initial modality.
choices.temptation: Extends the prior CTA technique to the unexamined lower segment because it offers more detail.
choices.counterfactual: New aneurysm-attributable symptoms would change the task to diagnostic cross-sectional imaging.

choices.label: Arrange no additional aortic imaging
choices.rationale: The study's caudal endpoint leaves the infrarenal aorta outside the acquisition. Smoking cessation does not negate the ever-smoker screening indication.
choices.temptation: Counts a study labeled aortic CTA as covering the entire aorta.
choices.counterfactual: A documented adequate full infrarenal study could make another screening examination unnecessary.

decisionNodes.stem: Which aortic surveillance schedule should have been selected for {patientName} after that comparison?

answerChoices.label: Abdominal aortic ultrasound every 12 months
answerChoices.rationale: The matched size places this asymptomatic man in the annual-ultrasound group.

answerChoices.label: Abdominal aortic ultrasound every 6 months
answerChoices.rationale: This follows a larger-AAA schedule rather than the supported schedule for his matched 4.7-cm diameter.

answerChoices.label: Abdominal aortic ultrasound every 3 years
answerChoices.rationale: This is too long for the measured 4.7-cm sac.

decisionNodes.explanation: The matched study establishes a 4.7-cm AAA, not a confirmed jump to 5.3 cm. Annual ultrasound is the guideline schedule for an asymptomatic man in this diameter band when ultrasound defines the sac adequately.

authorGate.cueAttack: The exhibit-free imaging record contains acquisition observations, not the conclusion 'measurement artifact.' The key is longest by a few words but all labels name a concrete imaging action; re-measure versus re-acquire is the tested distinction, not a caution cue.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Resolve the validity of a serial imaging comparison before any growth-based repair decision.
reasoningSteps: Identify noncomparable axial and centerline-perpendicular measurements.
Choose re-analysis of already acquired images rather than another acquisition or cross-modality comparison.
authorGate.difficulty: Moderate/hard: apparent threshold crossing tempts escalation, while a repeat scan feels more definitive than reviewing the adequate acquisition.
authorGate.decidingObservation: Different planes across a curved segment, with both datasets available.
authorGate.closestError: Repeat contrast CT under the same new axial protocol.
authorGate.consequence: Radiation/contrast exposure while leaving the growth inference unresolved.
authorGate.deletionTest: The whole update is required: removing the planes or availability of datasets changes the comparison. No report conclusion supplies the answer.
authorGate.counterfactual: If the original acquisitions were unavailable or inadequate for the needed landmarks, new appropriate cross-sectional acquisition would become reasonable.
authorGate.sequenceReview: Later annual-surveillance and symptom decisions receive new observations after this answer. This explanation does not specify an interval or symptom-triggered operation.
authorGate.repairAndRecheck: Rejected an initial immediate-repair foil because it compared another care stage. All three final choices address imaging validity; both new acquisitions have wait metadata.
