drafts.reviewDisplay: key shown first for review only

authorGate.cueAttack: The known genetic diagnosis is a legitimate prerequisite for this management objective; no approach is named as preferred in the presentation. All options are specific thoracoabdominal reconstructions of comparable scope, not an operation versus an obviously premature scan.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Definitive repair approach after the need for repair is established.
reasoningSteps: Recognize that native aortic sealing regions in heritable tissue disease differ from the degenerative anatomy commonly used for endovascular repair.
Apply that durability boundary and current operability to the approach preference.
authorGate.difficulty: Moderate/hard: technical feasibility and lower initial invasiveness make branched repair credible, and hybrid debranching may appear to remove the endograft durability issue.
authorGate.decidingObservation: Confirmed Marfan syndrome with native sealing regions and no prohibitive open risk.
authorGate.closestError: Branched endovascular repair because both procedures are technically feasible.
authorGate.consequence: Extending a degenerative-aneurysm procedural preference without accounting for the heritable substrate.
authorGate.deletionTest: Without the genetic/native-aorta findings, the preference is not established. Fitness and an already accepted repair indication prevent this becoming an unsupported size-threshold or surveillance question.
authorGate.counterfactual: Replace Marfan with a degenerative aneurysm and substantially elevated open operative risk: branched endovascular repair becomes a reasonable preferred alternative after aortic-team assessment.
authorGate.sequenceReview: Standalone exact context. No root/ascending threshold, prophylactic family surgery or traumatic injury objective is imported.
authorGate.repairAndRecheck: Removed an unverified exact diameter and a surveillance foil. Kept three actual reconstructions. The newer ESVS 2026 PDF was inaccessible; this single-guideline preference requires exact clinician review rather than claiming exhaustive current agreement.

explanation.text: For an intact TAAA requiring repair in Marfan syndrome, the checked multisociety guideline favors open repair. Native-aortic tissue disease and long-term durability matter even when branched or hybrid reconstruction is technically possible.

choices.label: Open thoracoabdominal graft replacement
choices.rationale: Heritable native-aorta disease in an operable patient favors open reconstruction when repair is required.
choices.temptation: Distinguishes the tissue disease from an ordinary degenerative aneurysm.
choices.counterfactual: Severe operative prohibitions or emergency bridging needs can change the balance.

choices.label: Branched endovascular thoracoabdominal repair
choices.rationale: Technical feasibility does not erase the guideline preference for open repair in this heritable native-aorta setting.
choices.temptation: Generalizes the lower initial invasiveness of endovascular repair to all aneurysm substrates.
choices.counterfactual: An appropriate degenerative TAAA patient with higher open risk may be considered for branched repair.

choices.label: Visceral debranching with thoracic endografting
choices.rationale: A hybrid operation still relies on endograft sealing in the diseased native aorta rather than providing the preferred open reconstruction.
choices.temptation: Assumes adding open visceral bypasses resolves the native-seal concern.
choices.counterfactual: Selected patients unsuitable for conventional open repair can require alternative hybrid strategies.

itemStatuses.parkedReason: A fair choice between specific urgent repair configurations requires verified device-specific anatomy/IFU or another directly supported discriminator. The existing generic suitable-anatomy claim cannot supply those criteria, and retaining its conclusion leaves a single guideline-preference rule.

Chronology can be clarified, but the review specifically requires clinician adjudication of decompression versus residual-branch embolization for the exact severity. No applicable clinician decision is recorded. Adding a fictional size threshold or asserting immediate superiority would not resolve that boundary.

The permitted CIRSE facts establish a wall-disruption treatment concern, but do not establish a unique technique among credible active procedures without further anatomy. A drainage-sequencing alternative would require an additional permitted source. The newly found i-EUS paper explicitly reserves AI/TDM rights and was excluded rather than used to supply that teaching point.

reviewFindings.title: Initial abdominal aortic screening

cues.phrase: he had never had abdominal aortic imaging
cues.why: Supplies the conclusion the learner was meant to draw from the chest acquisition boundary. It weakens the no-additional-imaging competitor before eligibility or modality is considered.

fairness: Ultrasound is the defensible best offered screening plan for this asymptomatic 69-year-old male ever-smoker. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
The subsequent ultrasound/repair decision follows coherently and is not disclosed by this explanation.
suggestions: Retain the actual prior scan coverage and remove the redundant conclusion about never having abdominal imaging. Reassess whether the remaining record requires a consequential coverage inference; otherwise seek explicit acceptance as foundational screening practice rather than claiming resident-level two-step difficulty.

Review scope: all 26 candidate nodes were assessed, including the two rewritten meanings and 24 new meanings. Ten retirement/replacement proposals and two unkeyed withheld decisions are noted but not scored; there are no kept-unchanged candidates. Findings use candidate visible content and prior candidate feedback, not author self-ratings. This is an offline editorial/clinical-plausibility review without fresh source verification; difficulty is predicted, and PASS is not Melissa Rowland's exact-version clinical approval. Runtime rendering, wait previews and source provenance were not independently validated.

reviewResponse.response: Removed the declaration that abdominal imaging had never occurred. The original acquisition actually ends at the celiac origin, so the resident must infer the unexamined infrarenal segment and then select the appropriate eligible-smoker screen. Prior coverage is necessary evidence rather than an unavailable-series inference. Predicted moderate; no basic-item exemption is claimed.

manualAuthorGate.cueAttack: Removed the conclusion that no abdominal imaging had ever occurred. The record now names a real acquisition endpoint that includes an upper abdominal segment. No label states whether that acquisition completed screening; all choices are concrete imaging plans.
manualAuthorGate.stageAndCategory: Initial preventive imaging plans after review of an existing aortic acquisition.
reasoningSteps: Infer from the celiac-level endpoint that the infrarenal survey remains incomplete despite a CTA title.
Apply ever-smoker eligibility and the preventive care phase to choose ultrasound rather than a diagnostic CTA or no study.
manualAuthorGate.difficulty: Fair moderate author prediction. Coverage interpretation now changes a credible no-imaging plan. A harder device or acute-care problem would change the established screening meaning; no foundational exception or measured difficulty is claimed.
manualAuthorGate.decidingObservation: The archived acquisition ends near the celiac origin rather than extending through the infrarenal aorta.
manualAuthorGate.closestError: No further imaging because an aortic CTA has already been performed.
manualAuthorGate.consequence: Leaving the intended abdominal screening territory unassessed.
manualAuthorGate.deletionTest: Without the caudal endpoint, completed prior screening cannot be decided. Age and smoking determine whether the incomplete survey matters. Removed the redundant never-imaged sentence.
manualAuthorGate.counterfactual: Extend the prior adequately visualized acquisition through the infrarenal aorta and document normal dimensions: no additional one-time screen becomes the best offered plan.
manualAuthorGate.sequenceReview: This v2 question is standalone. The PASS referral remains in its entire original v1 case with original earlier feedback; no new presentation or feedback is silently attached to that PASS.
manualAuthorGate.repairAndRecheck: Applied the independent review's specific deletion and re-solved all three plans. Kept a moderate boundary rather than inventing an unrelated difficult criterion.

reviewFindings.title: Outer sac diameter and repair referral
fairness: The learner must distinguish the aneurysm's outer diameter from its flowing channel and use that distinction to choose repair evaluation versus surveillance. The two sizes make the surveillance error concrete.
Symptoms, functional status and major competing illness are sufficiently addressed for a referral decision. No competing offered plan is equally appropriate.
The update is coherent after screening and contains the result needed to answer without recalling the prior choice. Prior screening feedback does not disclose the diameter rule.
suggestions: Retain the lumen-versus-sac discriminator and comparable action labels. Keep PASS separate from clinical approval.

reviewResponse.response: Exact original question, node, timing and complete original case preserved. Editorial PASS is scoped to the reviewed version and visible context; it is not named clinical approval.

reviewFindings.title: Reconciling different aortic measurement planes

cues.phrase: perpendicular to the aortic centerline
cues.why: The key repeats the earlier report's distinctive measurement phrase while the repeat-CT foil explicitly repeats the new axial protocol. The wording largely identifies the preferred correction.

cues.phrase: Both original CT datasets are available
cues.why: Availability is legitimate, but combined with the explicit plane mismatch and a task already requiring an imaging correction, it makes reuse of those datasets the only sensible offered action.

fairness: Reformatting and comparable orthogonal measurements are a defensible best answer. The issue is low discrimination rather than a demonstrated wrong key.
Elapsed time would be needed to judge a growth rate, but this task appropriately stops before that judgment. Do not invent a growth threshold.
suggestions: Make the resident interpret a concise measurement/acquisition exhibit and decide whether the apparent change warrants additional acquisition or a change in management. Compare credible approaches to the actual uncertainty rather than repeating the stated problematic protocol as a foil.
Preserve dataset adequacy and availability when necessary; removing those facts without replacing them would make retrieval versus repeat acquisition unfair.

reviewResponse.response: Replaced the repeated perpendicular phrase and deliberately repeated axial acquisition with an original acquisition/measurement table and a neutral next-plan task. Both acquired thin-section volumes are adequate. The six-month interval and directly checked growth recommendation make immediate repair assessment a credible competing policy if the change were real; the plane mismatch must first be resolved. No new acquisition is falsely claimed necessary.

manualAuthorGate.cueAttack: The neutral task no longer demands an imaging correction. A compact acquisition table supplies the actual planes and source-series adequacy; the key does not repeat a distinctive perpendicular phrase. Repair assessment and surveillance are genuine competing responses to the apparent change.
manualAuthorGate.stageAndCategory: Next aortic management plan after discordant serial reports, before a growth claim is accepted.
reasoningSteps: Interpret the relationship between vessel curvature, measurement plane and reported change.
Decide whether to verify the change now, apply a growth-based repair policy or apply a size-based surveillance band.
manualAuthorGate.difficulty: Moderate/hard prediction: both the apparent growth over six months and a subthreshold latest diameter invite defensible-looking but incompatible policies. Neither can be applied correctly until measurement validity is resolved.
manualAuthorGate.decidingObservation: Different image planes despite adequate complete source volumes from both time points.
manualAuthorGate.closestError: Repair referral based on the apparent six-month enlargement as if it were confirmed.
manualAuthorGate.consequence: Escalating care on an invalid comparison or overlooking a consequential trajectory by merely rescheduling surveillance.
manualAuthorGate.deletionTest: Removing the plane or source-volume rows changes the validity of the comparison. Removing the interval would make a growth-rate interpretation unfair; six months is now explicit.
manualAuthorGate.counterfactual: Make both values matched orthogonal outer-wall measurements at the same landmark: the confirmed six-month increase supports the offered repair-evaluation plan.
manualAuthorGate.sequenceReview: Later v2 nodes receive a reconciled comparison and a separate change in ultrasound adequacy, then a new pain episode. The explanation gives no later MRI or pain-attribution answer.
manualAuthorGate.repairAndRecheck: Replaced the deliberately repeated bad CT protocol foil with actual growth-versus-surveillance decisions. Added only the directly checked ACC/AHA growth boundary; no new automatic operation rule.

reviewFindings.title: Surveillance after matched AAA measurements
clarityIssues: The time between the two matched studies is not stated. The node should not imply that a growth-rate assessment has been completed from diameters alone.
fairness: Annual ultrasound is consistent with the intended uncomplicated male AAA diameter-band rule. The item supplies the corrected size and adequate ultrasound visualization, so selecting among intervals is essentially single-rule recall.

The sequence is coherent, but the preceding feedback has already taught the measurement correction. This node does not independently retest that inference, and the corrected current diameter alone selects the intended answer.
suggestions: If routine surveillance eligibility depends on the serial comparison, state its actual interval and relevant trajectory without inventing a growth cutoff.

Add a clinically consequential competing surveillance consideration or seek explicit acceptance as foundational interval practice. Do not count the prior node's measurement inference as this node's second step.

reviewResponse.response: Specified the earlier six-month matched trajectory and a later annual visit. Changed the scored meaning to current surveillance modality: acquired supine/lateral ultrasound views fail to trace the posterior sac, while a documented severe iodinated-contrast reaction competes with the usual CT response. MRI versus CTA versus another duplex are parallel investigations. Prior measurement feedback does not supply the modality answer. New concept ID retains the former interval identity separately.

manualAuthorGate.cueAttack: Removed the supplied adequate-ultrasound conclusion and the three interval labels. The raw acoustic-window observations and immediate contrast reaction are necessary constraints; all options are named aortic investigations with their own wait metadata.
manualAuthorGate.stageAndCategory: Complete a current nondiagnostic surveillance examination with an appropriate imaging modality.
reasoningSteps: Determine that the current examination cannot establish the full aneurysm dimension despite the prior stable comparison.
Select cross-sectional imaging while accounting for the serious prior iodinated-contrast response.
manualAuthorGate.difficulty: Moderate/hard prediction: repeating the customary surveillance modality and automatically escalating to CTA are each credible errors. The new clinical meaning is modality adequacy, so the old interval concept/history is retained separately.
manualAuthorGate.decidingObservation: The posterior sac boundary is not measurable on the current views, and the prior iodinated injection produced an immediate systemic reaction.
manualAuthorGate.closestError: Order CTA after correctly recognizing that ultrasound is inadequate.
manualAuthorGate.consequence: Unnecessary repeat exposure to the implicated contrast class, or failure to establish an interpretable aneurysm dimension.
manualAuthorGate.deletionTest: Remove the contrast reaction and CT becomes a supported alternative; remove the acoustic limitation and ordinary ultrasound remains appropriate. The actual six-month interval eliminates the original rate-assessment ambiguity.
manualAuthorGate.counterfactual: Provide complete reproducible current ultrasound visualization of the sac: duplex becomes the appropriate offered study despite the contrast history.
manualAuthorGate.sequenceReview: The preceding measurement feedback does not teach MRI selection. The later pain record uses MR angiography, maintaining the contrast-history chronology rather than silently performing another routine iodinated CTA.
manualAuthorGate.repairAndRecheck: Changed the scored meaning explicitly instead of claiming that a corrected diameter creates two new inferences. Verified ACC/AHA ultrasound/CT/MRI recommendations and retained the old meaning without FSRS transfer.

reviewFindings.title: New pain in a smaller intact AAA

cues.phrase: should have replaced surveillance
cues.why: The task rules out both surveillance options before the learner interprets the symptoms. Only the repair-evaluation answer can satisfy the wording.

cues.phrase: the hospital evaluation identifies no competing abdominal or spinal cause
cues.why: This broad authored exclusion further supplies the attribution instead of showing the observations that distinguish the closest competing explanation.

fairness: New persistent aortic-localized pain and tenderness support inpatient repair assessment despite intact imaging and a diameter below the usual asymptomatic threshold. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
The chronology clearly changes the earlier asymptomatic premise, and the update contains the new decision-critical findings. The task itself, however, defeats the options.
suggestions: Ask neutrally which plan was appropriate at that admission; remove the instruction that surveillance must be replaced.

Retain genuine safety findings and use concrete relevant evaluation findings instead of a blanket exclusion of other causes. Compare credible plans at that stage rather than one active plan against two unsupported delays.

reviewResponse.response: Made the admission task neutral, removed the blanket exclusion of all other causes, and supplied new pain at rest with positional persistence, focal mass tenderness and an unchanged chronic lumbar finding. The competing lumbar-imaging plan is a real alternative to vascular assessment; intact MR imaging does not make the symptoms an asymptomatic surveillance decision. MR angiography preserves the preceding contrast-reaction chronology. Fair moderate prediction rather than a claimed hard threshold recall.

manualAuthorGate.cueAttack: Removed 'should have replaced surveillance' from the task and the blanket claim excluding every alternative cause. The record instead gives a genuine competing lumbar observation, its chronology and the pain localization. Both alternative plans involve real assessment or follow-up.
manualAuthorGate.stageAndCategory: Current inpatient aortic-versus-spine/observation plans after a new pain evaluation.
reasoningSteps: Use the pain behavior, focal examination and unchanged lumbar image to assess the competing attribution.
Apply that attribution to inpatient vascular repair assessment rather than the earlier asymptomatic size policy.
manualAuthorGate.difficulty: Fair moderate prediction: an incidental spine abnormality and an intact aneurysm image are credible anchors. Diagnostic attribution remains a clinical judgment; the draft does not pretend that imaging alone proves the pain source.
manualAuthorGate.decidingObservation: New persistent rest pain is reproduced over the aortic mass while the competing lumbar structural finding is unchanged.
manualAuthorGate.closestError: Spine MRI first because a lumbar deformity appears in the imaging record.
manualAuthorGate.consequence: Delaying aortic assessment after a meaningful change in symptoms.
manualAuthorGate.deletionTest: Without the actual competing lumbar finding this is a simpler symptom-trigger rule. Without chronology and focal localization, choosing the vascular pathway would be less defensible. No blanket negative supplies the interpretation.
manualAuthorGate.counterfactual: Replace aortic tenderness/rest pain with reproducible mechanical back pain and new corresponding spinal findings: the spine-directed investigation becomes reasonable before attributing symptoms to the AAA.
manualAuthorGate.sequenceReview: Earlier feedback concerns imaging adequacy and does not rehearse pain as a repair indication. MR angiography preserves the serious iodinated-contrast history established in the preceding v2 node.
manualAuthorGate.repairAndRecheck: Re-solved the neutral task after deleting the cue and broad exclusion. Kept the supported moderate attribution problem rather than adding an unsourced imaging sign or compulsory operation deadline.

reviewFindings.title: Repair evaluation for an asymptomatic woman
fairness: Repair evaluation is a defensible offered plan at the stated size and functional status. This wording does not mandate a specific operation.

The exact strength of sex-specific size recommendations and the boundary with continued surveillance require clinician/source confirmation; this offline review does not establish a universal mandatory repair threshold.
As written, sex plus an explicitly established diameter selects a familiar threshold rule. Stable serial size adds a misconception but little independent interpretation.
suggestions: If retained as resident application, introduce a real competing consideration that changes the referral decision and is resolved by observations, rather than adding more statements of fitness.

Explain the actual source-supported recommendation and its limitations after answering. Preserve evaluation-versus-mandatory-operation distinctions and avoid presenting all women's thresholds as a universal rule.

reviewResponse.response: Replaced the established single diameter with an original outer-contour-versus-flowing-channel measurement exhibit. The resident must choose the relevant dimension before applying the sex-specific assessment boundary. Post-answer feedback and a new atomic comparison record the different ACC/AHA and SVS recommendation strength; referral for assessment is distinguished from mandatory operation or a selected technique. Source checks reconfirmed the exact female boundary and SVS range.

manualAuthorGate.cueAttack: The presentation no longer announces an established 5.1-cm aneurysm as a completed interpretation. The constructed table provides competing measured structures. All labels are concrete management plans with comparable grammar; no mandatory-operation or generic shared-decision key is used.
manualAuthorGate.stageAndCategory: Elective aortic management after a measurement record, before selecting any repair technique.
reasoningSteps: Identify the maximum full sac dimension rather than the residual flow channel.
Apply the female assessment boundary rather than the male threshold or the female interval for a smaller sac.
manualAuthorGate.difficulty: Moderate prediction: each surveillance choice follows a different credible error, so the learner must resolve both dimension and population. It is not claimed to be a universal mandatory operation rule.
manualAuthorGate.decidingObservation: A 5.1-cm outer contour surrounds a smaller flowing channel in a woman.
manualAuthorGate.closestError: Use the full size but apply a male threshold and defer assessment for six months.
manualAuthorGate.consequence: Postponing repair assessment or following the wrong sac-size band.
manualAuthorGate.deletionTest: Removing the contour/channel distinction leaves only threshold recall; removing sex makes the assessment-versus-six-month choice different. Extra fitness statements were not added to manufacture difficulty.
manualAuthorGate.counterfactual: Change the patient to a man with the same asymptomatic full dimensions: six-month ultrasound becomes an appropriate offered plan. Change the female full sac to 4.2 cm: annual follow-up becomes appropriate.

ACC/AHA recommends repair at the female size boundary, while SVS frames repair in the 5.0-5.4-cm range as a suggestion; both support specialist repair assessment in this supplied context. Neither diameter nor sex selects a procedure or removes the need to consider operative risk and patient goals.

choices.label: Arrange elective vascular repair assessment
choices.rationale: The full outer contour, not the flowing channel, reaches the female repair-assessment range. This supports evaluation rather than choosing an operation automatically.
choices.temptation: Integrates which dimension matters with the population-specific recommendation.
choices.counterfactual: A smaller full sac could instead support continued surveillance.

choices.label: Arrange aortic ultrasound in six months
choices.rationale: This can follow a male threshold applied to the full sac or a surveillance-only policy, but it postpones the supported female repair assessment here.
choices.temptation: Uses the familiar male boundary despite correctly reading the outer dimension.
choices.counterfactual: For an asymptomatic man with the same 5.1-cm full sac, six-month surveillance can be appropriate.

choices.label: Arrange aortic ultrasound in twelve months
choices.rationale: The 4.2-cm flowing channel is not the aneurysm's full dimension used for the female surveillance band.
choices.temptation: Applies the correct female interval to the wrong measured structure.
choices.counterfactual: An asymptomatic woman whose full sac, rather than flowing channel, measures 4.2 cm could have annual ultrasound.

record.title: Definitive treatment of infected graft-enteric communication
fairness: The learner must interpret persistent infection plus a graft-to-bowel channel and distinguish definitive source control from hemorrhage bridging or suppressive therapy.

Graft removal with vascular and bowel reconstruction is the defensible best offered definitive strategy in the stated operable patient. The alternatives can have roles in other settings, which makes stability and operability necessary information rather than gratuitous permission.

The update follows imaging coherently and contains enough current information to answer independently. Earlier feedback identifies concern for a complication but does not prescribe this definitive operation.
suggestions: Keep the explicit definitive-treatment task and persistent-infection observations. Do not imply that suppressive treatment or endovascular bridging has no role in inoperable or unstable patients.

contextAudit.cueRecheck: The new header does not label a graft-enteric diagnosis or prescribe an operation. The unchanged CTA/antibiotic-response update must be interpreted before ranking reconstruction against bridging or suppression. The operability boundary remains in the reviewed update.
contextAudit.sequenceRecheck: The diagnostic companion and all its feedback are absent. The definitive-source-control task refers to its own complete current update, so a prior imaging answer is not required.

authorGate.cueAttack: The new header does not label a graft-enteric diagnosis or prescribe an operation. The unchanged CTA/antibiotic-response update must be interpreted before ranking reconstruction against bridging or suppression. The operability boundary remains in the reviewed update.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Definitive source-control strategy after diagnostic confirmation, with antimicrobials common background care.
reasoningSteps: Recognize persistent prosthesis/bowel infection despite directed treatment rather than an isolated bloodstream episode.
Use current operative suitability to choose removal/reconstruction over bridging or suppression.
authorGate.difficulty: Hard: rapid endovascular control and antibiotic response can be mistaken for definitive treatment of an infected prosthesis.
authorGate.decidingObservation: A communicating perigraft collection, persistent same-organism cultures and no prohibitive operative condition.
authorGate.closestError: Covered relining as definitive treatment because it may arrest bleeding.
authorGate.consequence: Persistent infected material and bowel contamination.
authorGate.deletionTest: Without operative suitability, suppression or endovascular treatment may become defensible; without the persistent source, an immediate major reconstruction would not be established.
authorGate.counterfactual: Replace stable operability with uncontrolled hemorrhage and shock: covered relining as a bridge may become appropriate. Replace it with prohibitive permanent operative risk: suppression may be considered.
authorGate.sequenceReview: The diagnostic companion and all its feedback are absent. The definitive-source-control task refers to its own complete current update, so a prior imaging answer is not required.
authorGate.repairAndRecheck: Retain the type and timing of the prosthetic operation and its presenting syndrome. The exact node already supplies the CTA communication, persisting organism despite treatment, current perfusion and operability needed for the definitive strategy. Operative history, fever, recurrent cultures and melena come from the original header. The prior proximal-endoscopy record and diagnostic question are unnecessary to this treatment-stage decision and are omitted. Only the new standalone context and neutral final routing need independent recheck; no new PASS or clinical approval is asserted.

choices.label: Graft removal with arterial and bowel reconstruction
choices.rationale: The operable stable patient has an infected prosthesis with bowel communication; definitive surgery addresses the infected material and communication.
choices.temptation: Distinguishes definitive source control from bridging or suppression.
choices.counterfactual: Prohibitive operative risk could change the balance toward nonoperative suppression or a limited strategy.

choices.label: Covered endovascular relining across the affected graft
choices.rationale: Relining can bridge hemorrhage in instability or serve selected patients unsuitable for open surgery, but it leaves the infected prosthesis and bowel communication.
choices.temptation: Uses rapid bleeding control as though it establishes durable infection source control.
choices.counterfactual: Uncontrolled hemorrhage in an unstable patient can make an endovascular bridge reasonable.

choices.label: Retained graft with prolonged suppressive antimicrobial therapy
choices.rationale: Suppression does not remove the demonstrated source in this patient who can undergo definitive reconstruction.
choices.temptation: Equates a temporary physiologic response to antibiotics with eradication of an infected prosthesis.
choices.counterfactual: A patient who cannot tolerate reconstruction may need a suppression-based strategy after specialist review.

answerChoices.label: Aortography across the seal zones and graft junctions
answerChoices.rationale: The enlarging sac and uncertain source require reassessment for direct graft or attachment inflow before targeting a branch.

answerChoices.label: Aortography across the seal zones and graft junctions
answerChoices.rationale: The enlarging sac and uncertain source require reassessment for direct graft or attachment inflow before targeting a branch.

answerChoices.label: Selective mesenteric-to-inferior-mesenteric collateral angiography
answerChoices.rationale: This maps a branch route but does not resolve the possible attachment or component defect producing the current sac growth.

answerChoices.label: Selective iliolumbar-to-lumbar collateral angiography

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: Aortography shows arterial-phase contrast entering the sac between the main body and right iliac limb. Their fabric ends are separated rather than overlapped; the adjacent fabric is intact and the components remain aligned. Proximal and distal native-wall attachment images show no contrast escaping at those sites.
decisionNodes.stem: Which endovascular repair should have addressed {patientName}'s demonstrated leak?

answerChoices.label: Covered stent-graft bridging at the modular junction
answerChoices.rationale: A fabric gap provides a direct route into the sac. A covered bridge restores the missing barrier between the aligned components.

answerChoices.label: Balloon remodelling at the modular junction
answerChoices.rationale: Expansion can improve apposition where fabric overlaps, but cannot supply the absent covering between separated ends.

answerChoices.label: Bare-metal stent reinforcement at the leaking segment
answerChoices.rationale: Radial scaffolding does not add a covering across the demonstrated open channel to the sac.

decisionNodes.explanation: The problem is loss of covered continuity, not simply insufficient expansion. A covered bridge can close a separated modular junction. Balloon remodelling or bare-metal reinforcement addresses other apposition/support problems but does not itself cover a fabric gap.
sourceLabels: Joo-Young Chun et al. (2024). CIRSE Standards of Practice on Management of Endoleaks Following Endovascular Aneurysm Repair.

record.title: Reassessing an enlarging EVAR sac with uncertain inflow
fairness: The meaningful decision is to question the earlier branch-leak attribution when a larger sac and indeterminate graft-junction flow appear, then investigate a potential direct graft-related source before selective branch treatment.

The three choices are angiographic assessments at the same stage. Aortography is a defensible first offered assessment; selective collateral studies might subsequently be needed but do not replace assessment of the uncertain graft interface.

The update supplies the current uncertainty even if earlier feedback is not recalled. Prior advice that source and sac behavior matter is general scaffolding, not disclosure of this selected assessment.
suggestions: Retain the distinction between an earlier documented pattern and an uncertain current source. Do not convert the task into an unsupported universal rule that selective studies are never useful.

contextAudit.contextReason: The later 7.0-cm measurement needs an actual earlier diameter and prior source pattern. Move only those constructed observations into the presentation, without carrying the earlier surveillance answer or explanation.
contextAudit.carriedFacts: The 5.8-cm outer-sac value is from the original prior-node exhibit. Delayed lumbar-associated filling and intact attachments/overlaps are from the original header. No new measurement or growth cutoff is invented.
contextAudit.cueRecheck: The header gives the earlier observations without a type-II label or a treatment instruction. The current arterial/delayed acquisition remains indeterminate despite adequate phases, so source reassessment still competes with two credible selective branch studies.
contextAudit.sequenceRecheck: Both the prior stable-sac scored turn and the later component-repair turn are absent. Earlier raw measurements are supplied directly; no prior key or feedback is needed to interpret the changed source uncertainty.

authorGate.cueAttack: The header gives the earlier observations without a type-II label or a treatment instruction. The current arterial/delayed acquisition remains indeterminate despite adequate phases, so source reassessment still competes with two credible selective branch studies.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Define the inflow source during catheter workup before selecting targeted treatment.
reasoningSteps: Recognize that a new expanding sac invalidates automatic reassurance from prior stable branch flow.
Choose central graft/seal assessment before committing to one collateral route.
authorGate.difficulty: Hard prediction: the earlier correct surveillance decision and branch finding create a credible anchoring error; nearby lumbar contrast is not proof of causal inflow.
authorGate.decidingObservation: Large interval sac expansion plus artifact-limited origin near a graft junction despite an adequate multiphase acquisition.
authorGate.closestError: Targeted lumbar angiography as if the original attribution were still established.
authorGate.consequence: Missing a direct-pressure leak and treating the wrong pathway.
authorGate.deletionTest: Deleting the growth and new uncertainty restores the earlier surveillance rationale. Phase acquisition details distinguish actual ambiguity from a merely missing export.
authorGate.counterfactual: If multiphase imaging conclusively established isolated lumbar inflow with no attachment or junction defect, selective iliolumbar mapping would become reasonable for treatment planning.
authorGate.sequenceReview: Both the prior stable-sac scored turn and the later component-repair turn are absent. Earlier raw measurements are supplied directly; no prior key or feedback is needed to interpret the changed source uncertainty.
authorGate.repairAndRecheck: The later 7.0-cm measurement needs an actual earlier diameter and prior source pattern. Move only those constructed observations into the presentation, without carrying the earlier surveillance answer or explanation. The 5.8-cm outer-sac value is from the original prior-node exhibit. Delayed lumbar-associated filling and intact attachments/overlaps are from the original header. No new measurement or growth cutoff is invented. Only the new standalone context and neutral final routing need independent recheck; no new PASS or clinical approval is asserted.

answerChoices.label: Reconstruct the serial CT volumes for matched measurements
answerChoices.rationale: The apparent increase uses different planes. Adequate source volumes permit a valid comparison before using enlargement to determine repair assessment.

answerChoices.label: Refer for repair evaluation based on serial enlargement
answerChoices.rationale: The amount and interval would matter if the measurements were comparable, but the plane discrepancy prevents treating the reported difference as confirmed growth.

answerChoices.label: Schedule ultrasound follow-up using the latest reported size
answerChoices.rationale: Applying a surveillance band to the unreconciled latest value does not resolve whether a consequential interval change occurred.

decisionNodes.explanation: The reported 0.7-cm difference spans different measurement planes. Use the adequate acquired volumes to establish a matched comparison before interpreting growth. decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The matched CT measurements are 4.6 and 4.7 cm, six months apart. At the following annual surveillance visit, ultrasound displays the anterior wall but cannot trace the posterior sac boundary through bowel gas on the acquired supine and lateral views. During the last iodinated-contrast injection he developed wheezing, generalized hives and hypotension requiring epinephrine. He has no new pain.
decisionNodes.stem: Which study should have completed {patientName}'s current aortic surveillance assessment?

answerChoices.label: MRI of the abdominal aorta
answerChoices.rationale: The current ultrasound does not define full sac size; MRI provides cross-sectional assessment without requiring the iodinated-contrast exposure implicated in his prior reaction.

answerChoices.label: CT angiography of the abdominal aorta
answerChoices.rationale: Cross-sectional imaging addresses the inadequate ultrasound, but this proposed contrast examination disregards the serious prior immediate reaction when MRI is a supported alternative.

answerChoices.label: Duplex ultrasound of the abdominal aorta
answerChoices.rationale: The prior success of ultrasound does not establish a usable current outer-wall measurement through the documented acoustic limitation.

decisionNodes.explanation: Current ultrasound adequacy matters more than the fact that ultrasound was useful previously. Cross-sectional assessment is needed when the sac is not defined, and MRI is reasonable when CT is contraindicated. The earlier matched measurements do not establish the current sac size after an inadequate examination.
sourceLabels: Society for Vascular Surgery (undated). Patients with Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm (AAA).
Eric M. Isselbacher et al. (2022). 2022 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Aortic Disease.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: During a later outside admission he reports new deep abdominal and back pain beginning at rest and persisting through changes in position. Palpation over the pulsatile abdominal mass reproduces the pain. MR angiography measures the infrarenal sac at 4.9 cm without extravasation. A chronic lumbar wedge deformity has the same appearance as on older imaging. His pressure and lower-limb strength remain preserved.
decisionNodes.stem: Which plan should have been selected for {patientName} during that admission?

answerChoices.label: Inpatient vascular assessment for aneurysm repair
answerChoices.rationale: New focal aortic tenderness and persistent nonmechanical pain change the previously asymptomatic premise despite an intact image and smaller diameter.

answerChoices.label: Inpatient lumbar MRI before vascular assessment
answerChoices.rationale: The unchanged structural spine finding does not establish that it explains the new rest pain and focal pain reproduced over the aorta.

answerChoices.label: Clinical observation with scheduled aortic ultrasound follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Routine observation and surveillance do not address the new aneurysm-localized symptoms simply because the scan shows no leak.

decisionNodes.explanation: The pain pattern and focal tenderness make the aneurysm clinically concerning even though MR imaging shows no extravasation. The unchanged lumbar finding does not by itself explain this new syndrome. Inpatient vascular repair assessment is appropriate; a size-based asymptomatic surveillance rule does not settle this admission.
sourceLabels: Society for Vascular Surgery (undated). Patients with Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm (AAA).

decisionNodes.stem: Which additional endovascular action should have addressed {patientName}'s persistent renal perfusion defect?

answerChoices.label: Stent the obstructed left renal artery segment
answerChoices.rationale: The central problem has improved, but a fixed dissected branch lesion continues to impede perfusion.

answerChoices.label: Fenestrate the distal aortic dissection septum
answerChoices.rationale: This targets a persistent central dynamic pressure problem, whereas the demonstrated residual defect is fixed within the branch.

case.presentation: {patientName}, a 64-year-old man, attends clinic after an aortic hospitalization. The founder reviews the admission record: CTA shows a flap beginning just distal to the left subclavian artery, with no ascending involvement or extravasation. His pressure is 184/96 mm Hg and rhythm is sinus at 108/min. Both kidneys enhance, urine output is maintained, and the abdominal and limb examinations show no ischemic findings. He has no conduction disease, active bronchospasm or decompensated heart failure.

decisionNodes.stem: Which initial hospital treatment plan should have been selected for {patientName} at that assessment?

answerChoices.label: Intravenous esmolol, then nicardipine if pressure remains high
answerChoices.rationale: The observed extent and perfusion support initial medical treatment; rate/impulse control precedes added vasodilation.

answerChoices.label: Urgent thoracic endovascular stent-graft repair
answerChoices.rationale: The admission record has not demonstrated rupture, malperfusion or failure of medical treatment that would establish an immediate repair indication.

answerChoices.label: Urgent open descending aortic graft replacement
answerChoices.rationale: An open replacement is not the initial treatment for this uncomplicated descending presentation.

decisionNodes.explanation: The initial record shows descending dissection with preserved organ perfusion and no rupture. Start monitored medical impulse control. Intravenous beta blockade comes before additional vasodilation when pressure remains high and beta blockade is not contraindicated.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: After monitored infusion treatment, his heart rate and pressure fall and chest pain improves. Urine output then drops and creatinine rises from 1.0 to 2.5 mg/dL. Repeat CTA shows a compressed aortic true lumen at the renal origins and much weaker left renal enhancement. There is no rupture. The treating aortic team documents usable proximal sealing and iliac access anatomy for TEVAR.
decisionNodes.stem: Which aortic plan should have been selected after {patientName}'s new renal findings?

answerChoices.label: TEVAR with reassessment of renal perfusion
answerChoices.rationale: The combination of functional decline and new inflow compromise demonstrates a complication requiring intervention, with residual branch flow reassessed after entry sealing.

answerChoices.label: Continue impulse infusions with renal observation
answerChoices.rationale: Achieved pressure control does not resolve the new structural inflow compromise and renal deterioration.

answerChoices.label: Open descending replacement with renal reassessment
answerChoices.rationale: Open repair is a real treatment, but documented TEVAR suitability supports the less invasive central repair strategy in this setting.

decisionNodes.explanation: Improved pressure and pain do not negate new organ malperfusion. The functional and CTA changes warrant intervention; TEVAR can relieve central dynamic true-lumen compression, after which branch perfusion must be reassessed.

record.title: Persistent renal branch obstruction after central repair
fairness: The learner must distinguish a fixed intrabranch lesion from persistent central dynamic obstruction using the response to TEVAR, branch flap, nonvarying narrowing and pressure gradient, then select the corresponding intervention.

Branch stenting is the defensible best offered treatment. Septal fenestration is a credible competing mechanism-specific action; extending an already effective proximal repair does not address the demonstrated branch lesion.

The update restates the completed repair and residual findings sufficiently to stand alone. Prior feedback mentions central dynamic compression and reassessment but does not name the static lesion or its treatment.
suggestions: Retain the response-to-treatment observations and branch pressure evidence. The technical detail is justified by a consequential mechanism-specific action; do not add unsupported numeric gradients.

authorGate.cueAttack: The header gives no static/dynamic mechanism label and no branch-treatment answer. The unchanged response-to-treatment observations distinguish branch stenting from aortic fenestration or proximal extension.
authorGate.stageAndCategory: Adjunctive endovascular treatment after a completed central repair, with ongoing documented organ inflow compromise.
reasoningSteps: Use central lumen expansion plus unchanged intrabranch narrowing to distinguish a residual fixed lesion from the earlier central mechanism.
Select the branch target rather than repeat central sealing or pressure equalization.
authorGate.difficulty: Hard: recognizing the initial mechanism does not establish the cause of the residual deficit; the current response must revise the anatomic target.
authorGate.decidingObservation: Central expansion and entry sealing coexist with fixed renal flap narrowing and persistent gradient.
authorGate.closestError: Distal septal fenestration for presumed continued dynamic obstruction.
authorGate.consequence: Additional intervention at the wrong target while renal ischemia persists.
authorGate.deletionTest: Delete the post-TEVAR response and the initial central strategy may still be appropriate. Delete the persistent functional/pressure defect and an incidental branch flap would not establish a need for treatment.
authorGate.counterfactual: If the branch were patent but central true-lumen collapse and cycling flap prolapse persisted, a pressure-equalizing fenestration could become reasonable.
authorGate.sequenceReview: Neither prior scored turn nor its feedback is present. The complete post-TEVAR update independently supplies all anatomy and perfusion observations needed for the additional-action task.

Age, sex, clinic review and the recorded outside TEVAR course are retained. explanation.text: The response separates mechanisms: central true-lumen compression improved, but a fixed flap within the renal artery still limits perfusion. Branch stenting can treat that static lesion rather than repeating a successful central repair.

choices.label: Stent the obstructed left renal artery segment
choices.rationale: The central problem has improved, but a fixed dissected branch lesion continues to impede perfusion.
choices.temptation: Localizes the residual obstruction after observing the central repair response.
choices.counterfactual: If branch flow recovered after central true-lumen expansion, an additional renal stent would not follow from these findings.

choices.label: Fenestrate the distal aortic dissection septum
choices.rationale: This targets a persistent central dynamic pressure problem, whereas the demonstrated residual defect is fixed within the branch.
choices.temptation: Carries forward the original dynamic-compression mechanism despite the documented response.
choices.counterfactual: Persistent dynamic aortic flap-related obstruction after entry treatment can merit fenestration.

choices.label: Extend the thoracic graft over the proximal seal
choices.rationale: The entry is sealed and central true-lumen expansion has already occurred; a proximal extension does not treat the fixed renal segment.
choices.temptation: Assumes every perfusion failure after TEVAR reflects inadequate central sealing.
choices.counterfactual: An incompletely sealed entry with persistent central compression could require graft revision.

record.title: Surveillance after inadequate ultrasound and severe contrast reaction
fairness: MRI is the best offered study. The resident must recognize that an untraceable posterior sac boundary prevents a current diameter assessment, then account for the severe prior iodinated-contrast reaction when choosing cross-sectional imaging.

The prior CT measurements do not substitute for a current examination. Repeat duplex is less persuasive after the documented positional attempts, and routine CTA is less attractive after wheezing, hives and hypotension requiring epinephrine. These observations are decision-critical and should not be removed merely because they distinguish the choices.

The sequence advances explicitly to the following annual visit, repeats the pertinent matched measurements and states the absence of new pain. It can be answered from the shared presentation and current update without recalling the previous key. This is a practical, high-yield surveillance-modality decision.

No confident clinical inaccuracy is identified. The explanation should not be read as declaring all CT techniques categorically contraindicated: the offered comparator is iodinated-contrast CTA, and the safety and feasibility of alternative protocols are not tested.
suggestions: For editorial precision, remove the unsupported historical aside that ultrasound was useful previously; the visible earlier measurements were CT measurements. State the reusable adequacy principle directly. This aside does not change the offered best answer.

explanation.text: Current ultrasound adequacy matters more than the fact that ultrasound was useful previously. Cross-sectional assessment is needed when the sac is not defined, and MRI is reasonable when CT is contraindicated. The earlier matched measurements do not establish the current sac size after an inadequate examination.

choices.label: MRI of the abdominal aorta
choices.rationale: The current ultrasound does not define full sac size; MRI provides cross-sectional assessment without requiring the iodinated-contrast exposure implicated in his prior reaction.
choices.temptation: Uses current test adequacy and the actual previous contrast response rather than reusing a formerly adequate modality.
choices.counterfactual: If the full sac were visualized reproducibly on the current ultrasound, ultrasound surveillance would remain appropriate.

choices.label: CT angiography of the abdominal aorta
choices.rationale: Cross-sectional imaging addresses the inadequate ultrasound, but this proposed contrast examination disregards the serious prior immediate reaction when MRI is a supported alternative.
choices.temptation: Correctly escalates imaging after an incomplete study but ignores the acquisition-specific constraint.
choices.counterfactual: Without an important CT contraindication, CT is a supported way to define an inadequately visualized AAA.

choices.label: Duplex ultrasound of the abdominal aorta
choices.rationale: The prior success of ultrasound does not establish a usable current outer-wall measurement through the documented acoustic limitation.
choices.temptation: Applies the ordinary small-AAA modality without checking whether this examination can actually measure the sac.
choices.counterfactual: An adequate current acoustic window and complete outer-wall visualization support ultrasound follow-up.

decisionNodes.stem: Which angiographic assessment should precede targeted leak treatment for {patientName} now?

answerChoices.label: Aortography across the seal zones and graft junctions
answerChoices.rationale: The enlarging sac and uncertain source require reassessment for direct graft or attachment inflow before targeting a branch.

answerChoices.label: Selective mesenteric-to-inferior-mesenteric collateral angiography
answerChoices.rationale: This maps a branch route but does not resolve the possible attachment or component defect producing the current sac growth.

answerChoices.label: Selective iliolumbar-to-lumbar collateral angiography
answerChoices.rationale: The lumbar branch near the contrast focus does not establish that it is the only source.

decisionNodes.explanation: Do not carry forward a branch-leak label when a growing sac has an uncertain current inflow source. Problem-solving aortography can assess the attachments and modular junctions before choosing a branch-directed treatment.
sourceLabels: Joo-Young Chun et al. (2024). CIRSE Standards of Practice on Management of Endoleaks Following Endovascular Aneurysm Repair.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: Aortography shows arterial-phase contrast entering the sac between the main body and right iliac limb. Their fabric ends are separated rather than overlapped; the adjacent fabric is intact and the components remain aligned. Proximal and distal native-wall attachment images show no contrast escaping at those sites.
decisionNodes.stem: Which endovascular repair should have addressed {patientName}'s demonstrated leak?

answerChoices.label: Covered stent-graft bridging at the modular junction
answerChoices.rationale: A fabric gap provides a direct route into the sac. A covered bridge restores the missing barrier between the aligned components.

answerChoices.label: Balloon remodelling at the modular junction
answerChoices.rationale: Expansion can improve apposition where fabric overlaps, but cannot supply the absent covering between separated ends.

answerChoices.label: Bare-metal stent reinforcement at the leaking segment
answerChoices.rationale: Radial scaffolding does not add a covering across the demonstrated open channel to the sac.

decisionNodes.explanation: The problem is loss of covered continuity, not simply insufficient expansion. A covered bridge can close a separated modular junction. Balloon remodelling or bare-metal reinforcement addresses other apposition/support problems but does not itself cover a fabric gap.
sourceLabels: Joo-Young Chun et al. (2024). CIRSE Standards of Practice on Management of Endoleaks Following Endovascular Aneurysm Repair.
